papers.abstract: We consider locally finite-hopping Hermitian operators that admit radial-type transfer matrix sets in the sense of Sadel. We extend his spectral averaging formula from scalar spectral measures to matrix-valued spectral measures associated to a root matrix. This extension yields criteria for lower bounds on the multiplicity of absolutely continuous spectrum. As applications, we consider random decaying shell-matrix potentials on stair-like graphs with increasing-width wires and operators on the Bethe lattice. In both cases, we establish that absolutely continuous spectrum has almost surely infinite multiplicity.

papers.title: CaDO: Formal Verification-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Causal Dataset Repair and Generation
papers.abstract: High-quality causal reasoning datasets are essential for developing models with reliable causal understanding, particularly in specialized domains. However, existing datasets frequently suffer from incorrect annotations and structural imbalances, which can lead to biased predictions and limited generalization. To address this issue, we propose CaDO (Causal-Engine-Guided Multi-Agent Data Optimization), a multi-agent framework for automated diagnosis and repair of causal reasoning datasets. Our framework consists of three key stages: formal causal reasoning, multi-level diagnosis, and automated data repair and generation. First, a Formalizer Agent translates natural language questions into formal causal queries to minimize semantic deviations and make retrieval and verification more explicit and tractable. Second, a dual-level diagnosis mechanism employs independent Critic Agents to identify sample-level errors while analyzing query-type coverage and label distributions to detect dataset-level structural imbalances. Finally, the framework employs reusable repair operators grounded in formal causal semantics to correct erroneous samples, while Explorer and Expander Agent collaboratively produce diverse and semantically consistent new samples. Experimental results show that CaDO significantly outperforms the strongest of five data cleaning baselines in 16 out of 18 experimental settings, improving downstream model accuracy by up to 9.1%. Moreover, at least 95% of the samples flagged by CaDO are defective, and on CLadder, CaDO incorrectly modifies 92.2% fewer correct labels than an LLM-based judge, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/thisissyu/cado.

papers.title: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbb{Q}_p$
papers.abstract: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the $\mathfrak{m}_D$-adic filtration.

papers.title: RAPID: Reconstruction Accelerated by Polarization-Informed Depth for 2D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Efficient and accurate 3D surface reconstruction from multi-view images remains a fundamental challenge in Gaussian splatting. Many existing methods rely on sparse geometric initialization and iterative densification, resulting in substantial optimization overhead and difficulties in balancing rendering quality and geometric accuracy, particularly in reflective and weakly textured regions. To address these limitations, we propose RAPID, a geometry-first framework that uses multiview polarization cues to recover dense surface priors. We integrate surface normals into depth maps using sparse geometric anchors. These depth maps are then fused across views. Curvature-adaptive sampling and oriented Gaussian initialization then support efficient optimization. Experiments on the PISR dataset demonstrate an approximately \(5\times\) speedup over PhyGaP, which is a state-of-the-art Gaussian-based reconstruction method. RAPID reduces the average optimization time from approximately 21 minutes (PhyGaP) to 4 minutes while maintaining competitive novel-view synthesis quality and mesh reconstruction accuracy. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of RAPID in accelerating Gaussian optimization from polarimetric multi-view inputs.

papers.title: Global nonsolvability of the leafwise $\dbar$-equation on foliations with Stein leaves
papers.abstract: Motivated by our previous work on $q$-convexity and global solvability for Levi flat structures, we study the complex foliation associated with the non-tame family of Stein structures constructed by Forstneri\v c and Sigurðardóttir. Although every leaf is closed and biholomorphic to $\C^2$ and the foliation admits a complete bundle-like Riemannian metric, there exists a smooth leafwise $\dbar$-closed $(0,1)$-form for which the leafwise $\dbar$-equation admits no global $L^r_{\loc}$ solution for any $0<r\le\infty$. This result also suggests a modification of Questions~2.10.4--2.10.6 in \emph{Foliations: Dynamics, Geometry and Topology}.

papers.title: Design-Based Inference for Fuzzy Difference-in-Differences
papers.abstract: I study fuzzy difference-in-differences designs from a design-based perspective, in which potential outcomes and treatment decisions are fixed and only the assignment of a policy is random, with heterogeneous and possibly unknown assignment probabilities. The Wald-DiD design estimand equals an assignment-weighted complier effect plus contamination from switchers, from changes in always-takers' effects and from trends in untreated outcomes. I derive the conditions under which the estimand holds a clear causal interpretation. The conditions are weaker than parallel trends in both outcomes and treatments. We propose an Anderson--Rubin-type test with a conservative Neyman variance that remains valid under weak first stages, a sensitivity analysis for the complier effect, and estimators for designs with known assignment probabilities. An application to the Oregon Health Insurance Experiment illustrates the results.

papers.title: Reliable Tree Recruitment from Scarce Annotations for Forest Inventory Expansion
papers.abstract: Species-level inventories of individual tree crowns (ITCs) from UAV imagery are limited by annotation cost: in tropical forests, many species are represented by only a handful of field-validated crowns. We propose a reliable tree recruitment framework that expands a small annotated inventory by iteratively self-training a multi-task DeepLabV3 network, combining semantic segmentation with a crown-distance regression head, on RGB UAV orthomosaics. At each iteration, candidate crowns enter the training inventory only if they pass a confidence filter on class probability and distance map and a morphology filter on crown area and solidity, with at most five new crowns per species, keeping recruited samples consistent with the reference inventory. We evaluate the framework at two Brazilian sites: an Amazonian rainforest in Acre (17 species, 355 annotated crowns, 4 cm GSD) and a forest site in the Cerrado of Maranhão (4 species, 51 annotated crowns, 1.8 cm GSD). Over 20 iterations, the number of retained crowns grew from about 500 to 960 in Acre and from about 700 to over 3100 in Maranhão, while crown-level F1 exceeded single- and multi-task DeepLabV3 baselines (53.5% vs. 50.0% and 45.2%; 92.2% vs. 79.7% and 83.6%). The framework offers a low-cost route to expanding species inventories with consumer-grade UAVs and limited fieldwork.
authors: Heitor Eduardo Ferreira Campos Morato Filpi

papers.title: Impact-Based Analysis Method (IBAM) to evaluate the primary stability of the pedicle screw: A proof of concept
papers.abstract: The long-term success of spinal instrumentation depends on the initial stability of pedicle screws (PS), yet current intraoperative assessments rely on surgeon subjectivity. This study introduces a quantitative, non-invasive approach-the Impact-Based Analysis Method (IBAM)-to support intraoperative decision-making. The IBAM measures screw stability using low-amplitude impacts delivered with an instrumented hammer on the surgical screwdriver after screw insertion. An IBAM indicator, defined as the average time difference between the two earliest local maxima in the force signal, was analyzed under varying stability conditions in artificial bone samples. Experimental factors included bone density ($ρ$), insertion depth ( D ), and pilot hole diameter ( $Φ$ ). The IBAM indicator was compared with the PS pull-out force for each configuration. Although the main effects showed opposite trends for the pull-out force and the IBAM indicator, their relative magnitudes were similar ( $ρ$ $\sim$35%, D $\sim$25%, $Φ$ $\sim$15%). The relationship between the pull-out force and the IBAM indicator followed a power-law model (adjusted R 2 =___0.85) with a negative exponent. As screw stability increased, the pull-out force rose while the IBAM indicator decreased, demonstrating complementary sensitivity to bone-implant interface changes. While results are promising, the simplified experimental design limited the ability to fully capture bone-implant interaction complexity. Future studies should aim to validate IBAM in vivo to confirm its clinical applicability..

papers.title: Stabilized negative viscosity governs ocean jets before, during and after they leave the coast
papers.abstract: Eddies in rotating turbulence can feed the jets that spawn them, resulting in the negative viscosity phenomenon. Taken alone, a negative viscosity represents up-gradient eddy fluxes and is often referred to as "antifriction" or "antidiffusion". Mathematically, it leads to an ill-posed problem. In two-dimensional turbulence theory, this problem can be resolved by representing the transfer from small to large scales by a stabilized negative viscosity (SNV), in which a negative Laplacian viscosity is balanced by its positive biharmonic counterpart. In purely two-dimensional turbulence, by the Taylor identity, a negative viscosity is up-gradient transport of vorticity, which mixing cannot produce; on a slope, mixing of potential vorticity can mimic it, and we test for this. Using two years of wide-swath satellite altimetry (SWOT), we measure the eddy momentum flux across the five subtropical western boundary currents in each current's own frame. Along the continental slope the eddies act with a negative viscosity of order $-10^{3}$ m$^{2}$ s$^{-1}$, with the SNV structure resolved in the Gulf Stream and the Agulhas. At separation from the slope the sign reverses in all five currents, and the eddies brake the flow. Downstream, in the free jets, the negative viscosity returns on the cyclonic flank, strengthened to $-10^{4}$ m$^{2}$ s$^{-1}$. Separation is where the current leaves the strong topographic $β$ of the slope, the constraint that orders the eddy transfer. In an eddy-resolving reanalysis the SNV form holds across three ocean basins, with its shape parameter set by the deformation radius.

papers.title: ScaleBench: An Extensible and Reproducible Experimental Platform for Kubernetes Autoscaling Research
papers.abstract: Autoscaling enables cloud-native applications to meet their SLOs by dynamically adjusting computational resources at runtime. Recent research has explored a broad range of advanced autoscaling approaches, including rule-based, optimisation-based, and machine learning-based techniques, to address the limitations of traditional resource management strategies in cloud-native environments. Despite significant advances, a considerable gap remains between academic innovations and their practical adoption in real-world environments. For instance, Kubernetes deployments commonly rely on the reactive, CPU-based Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, limiting the adoption of more advanced autoscaling approaches. Recent studies have investigated challenges such as autoscaler configuration and reproducible performance evaluation; however, the practical deployment, integration complexity, and operational overhead of research-based autoscalers in Kubernetes environments have received limited attention. To address this gap, we present ScaleBench, a native Kubernetes experimental platform to enable extensible and reproducible evaluation of autoscaling solutions. Unlike existing approaches, ScaleBench integrates autoscalers as native Kubernetes components, allowing researchers to assess not only scaling performance but also deployment characteristics and integration requirements within realistic cloud-native environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ScaleBench by evaluating multiple autoscaling approaches through a case study. The results highlight its capability to support systematic, repeatable, and practical assessment of Kubernetes autoscaling approaches.

papers.title: Asgard/NOTT: L-band nulling interferometry at the VLTI IV. Prospects for characterising hot exozodiacal dust
papers.abstract: Near-infrared interferometric surveys have revealed extended emission around the photosphere of $\approx 40$ main-sequence stars, attributed to the presence of hot exozodiacal dust (HEZD). A promising technique for investigating this phenomenon is nulling interferometry. The Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) nulling interferometer NOTT (Nulling Observations of exoplaneTs and dusT) is designed to characterise exoplanets and HEZD in the $L'$ band ($3.5-4.0\,μ$m). We aim to assess NOTT's potential for the detection and characterisation of HEZD with various instrumental and model parameter configurations. We model the HEZD as an optically thin dust ring, using the nearby Sun-like star $τ$ Ceti with HEZD as a reference model. Applying the end-to-end nulling tool SCIFYsim to model the instrumental response of NOTT to simulated HEZD brightness distributions, we evaluate how variations in HEZD and instrumental parameters affect NOTT's key observables: the photon flux rate and the null depth. We demonstrate that NOTT is capable of disentangling stellar and dust contributions to the signal and detecting HEZD. The null depth and photon flux rate are sensitive to the HEZD geometry, with inclination, position angle, and ring location having the strongest impact on the signal. Although the detailed temporal signatures are target-specific, the results can be generalised to other systems. NOTT has the potential to deliver unprecedented sensitivity for HEZD observations, granting access to detailed information through spectral dispersion, beam-combination schemes, and exploitation of sky rotation. This enables more sensitive HEZD detections than is possible with current instruments, and improved spatial constraints on the dust, as well as variability studies.

papers.title: Cohomological Foundations of Entropic Monotonicity: The Relative Cyclic Complex, the Transgression Map, and the Entropic $c$-Theorem in $d = 2$
papers.abstract: We develop a cohomological framework for the entropic $c$-theorem in two dimensions, based on the relative cyclic complex of a pair of von Neumann algebras and on the transgression map associated with a faithful normal state. The framework identifies the positivity underlying the entropic proof as Borchers positivity of the zero-frequency component of the relative modular cocycle, which is the operator-algebraic origin of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC). The positivity results are dimension-independent: they depend only on the split property, modular $p$-nuclearity, and the half-sided modular inclusion structure. The main results of the paper are: (i) the identification of the entanglement cohomology with the kernel of the restriction map (Theorem 2.6); (ii) Borchers positivity of the relative modular cocycle (Proposition 3.8}); (iii) the finite-dimensional positivity of the entropy flux (Corollary 3.9); and (iv) the entropic $c$-theorem in $d = 2$ (Theorem 4.3), which follows from (iii) and the one-variable analysis. The $c$-theorem proof uses no ultraviolet regulator at any intermediate step. We also formulate two open problems: the cochain-level positivity of the transgression (Conjecture 3.5) and the cohomological interpretation of the QNEC (Conjecture 3.11). Both are stated as research directions, not as results of the paper; in particular, the $c$-theorem proof does not depend on either of them. The extension of the framework to the $F$-theorem in $d = 3$ and the general-$d$ program is the subject of the companion paper \cite{Rashkov:2026b}.

papers.title: RSIBench-Infra: Can Agents Optimize Their Own Training and Inference Infrastructure at Production Scale?
papers.abstract: Improving the efficiency of training and inference infrastructure is a practical component of recursive self-improvement. Existing benchmarks for agent-driven optimization largely focus on individual software layers such as kernel, leaving unclear whether agents can deliver end-to-end performance gains under production workloads. We introduce RSIBench-Infra, a benchmark of 20 training and inference tasks spanning diverse model families and modalities, with deployments of up to 32 accelerators on NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Agents start from runnable baselines derived from official recipes and can modify the software stack across engine, kernel, and instruction levels. An OCI image-layer submission protocol captures these changes for reproducible deployment, while independent evaluation measures end-to-end performance under task-specific quality constraints. Across all task results, 66.2% exceed $1.10\times$ validated speedup. These results demonstrate that current agents can improve production-scale training and inference performance, but identifying effective optimization strategies and consistently translating local improvements into end-to-end gains remain challenging.

papers.title: Temporal Rank in Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are a natural framework for temporal modelling, yet are often dismissed due to their sequential, non-parallelisable computation and difficulty in capturing long-range dependencies, typically attributed to vanishing and exploding gradients. We identify a distinct and under-explored limitation: an information bottleneck induced by rank-constrained hidden state dynamics, which limits the number of independent input directions that can be preserved over time, as reflected in the rank of the input-to-state mapping. We show that this constraint restricts temporal capacity independently of gradient stability. To address this, we introduce structured high-dimensional state dynamics that preserve temporal separability and prevent saturation of the input-to-state Jacobian over time. On controlled sequence tasks, the resulting model exhibits rapid learning despite remaining strictly within a standard RNN formulation. Our results demonstrate that RNN performance is governed by the evolution and preservation of temporal rank, and suggest that mitigating gradient pathologies alone is insufficient without explicitly maintaining temporal capacity.

papers.title: Unveiling the Central Black Hole of NGC 3862: A Direct Mass Determination Using ALMA's High-Resolution Molecular Gas Kinematics
papers.abstract: We present the direct dynamical measurement of the supermassive black hole (SMBH) mass in NGC 3862 (3C 264), a massive Fanaroff-Riley type I radio galaxy. Using ALMA $^{12}$CO(2-1) observations, we map the cold molecular gas kinematics in the circumnuclear disk and model them with the KinMS forward-modeling code. The $^{12}$CO(2-1) disk exhibits a nearly face-on, ring-like morphology with regular disk rotation and a steep central velocity rise, providing clean dynamical constraints on the central gravitational potential. Our best-fit model yields $M_{\rm BH} = 2.40^{+0.52}_{-0.32}[{\rm stat.}] \pm 0.91 [{\rm sys.}] \times 10^9~M_\odot$ and a stellar mass-to-light ratio of $M/L_{\rm F814W} = 4.11^{+0.99}_{-0.27}[{\rm stat.}] \pm 0.17 [{\rm sys.}]~M_\odot/L_\odot$ (both at $1σ$ confidence level). This dynamically derived $M/L_{\rm F814W}$ consistent with an old, metal-rich stellar population and a Salpeter IMF. The SMBH sphere of influence is spatially resolved, confirming the robustness of our measurement. This places NGC 3862 among SMBHs with direct molecular gas dynamical constraints, contributing to the census needed to calibrate SMBH-host galaxy co-evolution models at the high-mass end of the scaling relations.

papers.title: Mesh Sensitivity of Different Boundary Treatments in High-Order Compact Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Hypersonic Heat-Flux Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate wall-heat-flux prediction in hypersonic flow depends on both the wall treatment and the available near-wall resolution. This work compares three complete implementations of a gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) for Mach~8.03 laminar flow over an isothermal circular cylinder: a linear Green--Gauss scheme (GG), a compact ghost-cell scheme (GC), and a pointwise one-sided compact scheme (POS). In POS, the stationary isothermal-wall conditions are imposed at the two Gaussian points used by the kinetic wall-flux quadrature. A reference mesh and six meshes in the uniform reduction (UR), log-layer unpacked (LLU), and log-layer packed (LLP) families are used to assess heat-flux sensitivity. At 24 digitized experimental angles, GG has the lowest root-mean-square difference on the reference, UR, and LLP families, whereas POS is closest on the two LLU meshes; GC is not the lowest-RMS scheme on any tested mesh. Hence no treatment is uniformly superior. On the present high-aspect-ratio cylinder grids, GG is the more robust choice except under LLU node redistribution, for which POS is preferable. Uniform reduction produces the largest heat-flux response for all three implementations. The comparison concerns complete schemes and does not isolate the pointwise constraints from differences in reconstruction and geometry representation.

papers.title: Structure and Thermal Conductivity of Epoxy-Graphene Oxide Composites from 4.5 to 300 K
papers.abstract: The microscopic mechanisms of heat transport in structurally disordered polymer-carbon composites remain incompletely understood, particularly over the broad temperature range extending from cryogenic to ambient conditions. Here, we investigate the relationship between structural organization and thermal transport in epoxy-graphene oxide (GO) composites with nominal GO contents of 0.25-10 wt.% relative to the resin (0.21-6.1 wt.% of the total composite mass). X-ray diffraction reveals predominantly amorphous scattering without a detectable GO(001) reflection, suggesting substantial suppression of ordered GO stacking within the cured epoxy matrix. Raman spectroscopy confirms the increasing contribution of the carbon phase while revealing no pronounced changes in the characteristic vibrational bands of the epoxy network. Thermal-conductivity measurements (4.5-300 K) demonstrate that GO incorporation modifies the temperature dependence of heat transport rather than producing a simple conductivity enhancement. The experimental data are described by a phenomenological multichannel model comprising a temperature-independent plateau term and two or three effective Arrhenius-type contributions characterized by distinct temperature scales ranging from a few to several hundred kelvin. The low-temperature conductivity plateau observed at lower GO concentrations is no longer resolved in GO-6 and GO-10, indicating a qualitative change in the temperature dependence of heat transport. These results establish a correlation between structural organization and the redistribution of effective thermal-transport contributions in epoxy-GO composites, providing an experimental basis for further microscopic interpretation within the framework of unified vibrational thermal-transport theory.

papers.title: Numerical integration of non-local master equations for renewal shot noise with drift and state-dependent amplitude
papers.abstract: The probability density of a system driven by a drift and a renewal train of kicks with state-dependent amplitude obeys a master equation that is non-local in space, because the kick operator $\hat{p}(i\partial_x I(x))$ is of infinite order, and, for non-exponential waiting times, non-local in time, with a memory kernel containing the propagator of the drift. Its solutions contain quasi-singular components, the never-kicked mass, which collapse onto the attractors of the drift. We present an accurate numerical method for such equations. The kick operator is a push-forward along the Marcus flow; in the Lamperti variable it becomes a translation, whose exact cell-to-cell weights follow from the cumulative distribution of the kicks, without quadrature. The drift is integrated by a conservative semi-Lagrangian step exact in time. The memory is represented by a sum of exponentials whose auxiliary fields are advected by the drift, at a cost linear in the number of steps. The never-kicked mass is transported exactly. For each ingredient we quantify the errors of simpler alternatives. The method is verified against exact solutions and event-driven Monte Carlo simulations with exact flow maps, from which it is statistically indistinguishable with $10^8$ trajectories. Parameters tuned for Gaussian kicks carry over unchanged to other kick distributions, and near a zero of the coupling, where the density vanishes faster than any power, the solution follows the known asymptotic law down to densities of order $10^{-37}$, far beyond Monte Carlo reach. As an application we compare the exact equation with its local and Poissonian approximations: in the range explored, the local equation deviates by up to 8% of the density width, also for waiting times with finite mean, consistently with an error estimate predicting larger deviations for slow drifts at long times. A Fortran implementation is available.

papers.title: Phase factors and optimal seminorms for polynomial averages of commuting transformations
papers.abstract: For invertible commuting measure-preserving transformations $T_1, \ldots, T_\ell$ on a standard probability space, we study polynomial averages along both integers and primes. We provide a rank-based criterion ensuring that, even when the polynomials are linearly dependent, finite-order phase factors are characteristic factors. For polynomials with integer coefficients and zero constant terms, it suffices that the dimension of the space spanned (over $\mathbb{Q}$) by any nonempty subfamily of $k$ polynomials exceeds $k/2$. These phase factors are generated by polynomial phases associated with positive integer powers of the individual transformations and may be strictly smaller than the corresponding Host-Kra factors of the same order. The required order depends only on the number of polynomials and their maximum degree. A four-term example involving a totally ergodic Heisenberg nilsystem shows that this criterion may fail if the equality $k/2$ is permitted. For a family of three polynomials, this criterion is equivalent to the condition that the polynomials are pairwise linearly independent. Consequently, it applies to the family $t, t^2, t^2+t$, where the third polynomial is the sum of the first two. For this specific family, we prove that the optimal orders for the phase factors and the Host-Kra factors are $4, 2, 2$, respectively--a result that holds for both integers and primes. The corresponding optimal seminorms are $U^5(T_1)$, $U^3(T_2)$, and $U^3(T_3)$, which provides an answer to a question posed by Kuca.

papers.title: $k-$Absorbing factorization in multiplicative lattices
papers.abstract: We study the multiplicative $C-$lattices generated by principal elements in which every proper element is a finite product of $k-$absorbing elements. We prove that such lattices have Krull dimension at most one. In the modular case, a finite direct product decomposition theorem is obtained.

papers.title: Radio emission from a local Little Red Dot: a challenge to the ionized cocoon scenario
papers.abstract: Several scenarios have been proposed to explain the properties of Little Red Dots (LRDs), invoking either heavy obscuration by dense neutral gas, super-Eddington accretion, or an ionized gas cocoon that produces electron scattering. Radio observations can distinguish between these scenarios. Radio emission is largely unaffected by neutral gas and dust obscuration, whereas free-free absorption can suppress it in the presence of large free electron columns. Here, we investigate the origin of radio emission from the local LRD J1047. We jointly analyze its radio data and the broad H$α$ emission from optical spectroscopy to test the predictions of different physical scenarios. We find that the observed radio luminosity must have an AGN origin, and it is consistent with that of a standard radio-quiet AGN obscured by dense neutral gas. Pure super-Eddington accretion underpredicts the radio luminosity by a factor of $\sim 30$, although a combination of super-Eddington accretion and obscuration remains viable. Interestingly, the statistically preferred model for the H$α$ profile is an exponential fit, which is often associated with electron scattering in LRDs. This interpretation implies an electron column density of $N_e=2.4\times10^{24}\rm~cm^{-2}$ and a strong free-free absorption ($τ_{\rm ff,5GHz}\sim 10^6$), incompatible with the radio detection. This tension suggests that the exponential profiles of J1047 more likely trace a stratified broad line region rather than electron scattering, with potential implications for virial black-hole mass estimates also in high-$z$ LRDs. Less likely, the radio emission may escape through a partially covering ionized medium or originate outside the putative scattering cocoon.

papers.title: Even Faster Algorithms for Bounded Integer Programming
papers.abstract: We study integer programs $\min\{\mathbf{c}^{T}\mathbf{x}: A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b},\mathbf{l}\le\mathbf{x}\le\mathbf{u},\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{Z}^n\}$ with a fixed number $d$ of equality constraints and constraint coefficients of absolute value at most $N$. Chen, Mao, and Zhang recently solved such programs in almost $N^{2d}$ time. We show that any polynomial saving for $(\min,+)$-convolution carries over to this problem. If witnessed $(\min,+)$-convolution of arrays of length $m$ can be computed in $\tilde{O}(m^ρ)$ time with error probability $p$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ bounded integer programming can be solved in $\tilde{O}\bigl(n+N^{(\max\{ρ,3/2\}+\varepsilon)d}\bigr)$ time with the same error probability $p$, up to polynomial factors in the encoding length and the cost of one linear program. A deterministic convolution algorithm yields a deterministic integer programming algorithm. Combined with recent truly subquadratic algorithms for $(\min,+)$-convolution, this gives a deterministic algorithm running in $\tilde{O}(n+N^{1.99986\,d})$ time and a randomized algorithm running in $\tilde{O}(n+N^{1.9602\,d})$ time, up to the same factors.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for Online TSP on the Half-Line
papers.abstract: In the open online traveling salesperson problem, requests appear over time at different positions of a metric space. A single agent traveling at unit speed must serve all requests, by visiting their positions, with the objective of minimizing the completion time. We propose online algorithms for this problem for the case that the metric space is the half-line. First, we present a $2$-competitive algorithm in which the server always either moves at unit speed or remains stationary, which improves on the previously best-known ratio of $2.04$. We further observe that algorithms must sometimes move slower than unit speed to achieve competitive ratios below $2$. We introduce a second algorithm that beats the barrier of $2$ by carefully modulating its speed, and prove a tight bound of $1.75$ on its competitive ratio. Finally, we slightly strengthen a known lower bound on the best-possible competitive ratio on the half-line from $1.627$ to $1.646$.

papers.title: Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models
papers.abstract: In active object detection, selecting the initial labeled pool is essential, especially in complex datasets with expensive labeling and low resource budget. This study presents an active learning framework designed to optimize the initial training cycle of active learning for the object detection task. Our approach diverges from traditional methods by utilizing feature-based clustering from the YOLO-World model and refining images based on objectness scores rather than relying on uncertainty sampling in the initial cycle. This approach focuses on finding samples with various features and emphasizes training in areas where the foundation model is most confident. Doing so helps the model better understand different types of objects. For subsequent cycles, we employ a consistency-based sampling technique to maintain the robustness of the training process. To evaluate our method, we use two complex datasets called Aquarium and NWPU VHR-10, which are well known for their diverse object sizes and challenging conditions. In the NWPU dataset, our method increases mAP50 by an average of 6.6% in image-based evaluation. Moreover, the image refinement method shows an improvement of approximately 11% in object-based evaluation. The results show improvements in model performance and labeling time, demonstrating the advantages of using foundation models in early cycles of active learning. An implementation of the algorithm is available at https://github.com/Mhrshd-fllh/ALBoost-FM

papers.title: What Majority Labels Hide: Annotator Disagreement and Model Errors in Multi-Dialect Arabic Sexism Detection
papers.abstract: Judgements of sexism are subjective and may vary across communities, yet sexism detection datasets usually reduce annotator judgements to a single majority label, obscuring disagreement and how models behave on contested cases. We introduce MuDAS, a dataset of YouTube comments in Saudi, Egyptian and Moroccan Arabic, each labelled by three native speakers of its dialect, with the individual annotations preserved. We use it to evaluate Arabic encoders fine-tuned with hard-label, soft-label and perspectivist objectives, GPT-5.6 Terra, and four Arabic-centric large language models. Model errors are more frequent on comments with annotator disagreement. Despite relatively close Macro-F1 scores, GPT-5.6 Terra and the fine-tuned encoders exhibit contrasting error patterns: GPT-5.6 Terra, even with the annotators' definition of sexism, over-classifies gender-related content such as religious advice on modesty, whereas the encoders miss implicit and prescriptive sexism. The Arabic-centric models also over-predict sexism and remain below the encoders. Disagreement-aware learning preserves Macro-F1, but soft labels improve alignment with annotators on contested comments at the expense of unanimous ones, and neither paradigm reliably identifies contested comments. Lower performance on Egyptian Arabic, clearest for the large language models, is not fully explained by the examined measures of test-set composition and dialectness. Majority-label scores can therefore hide contrasting error patterns that matter for content moderation.

papers.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
papers.abstract: For every \(1<p\le2\), we prove that the optimal universal factor relating the Enflo type \(p\) constant to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant is \(p\), already among finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. Ivanisvili, van Handel, and Volberg [Ann.\ of Math.\ (2) \textbf{192} (2020), 665--678] proved the equivalence with factor \(π/\sqrt{2}\). Areshidze [arXiv:2609.32666v1 (2026)] improved the upper bound to \(p\). Our matching lower bound settles the optimality question posed in that preprint. We also obtain two results for a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] For \(1<p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] For \(1<p\le2\), uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} These results show how Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality reduce the linear estimates needed to establish a metric type property of the whole space.

papers.title: How to Turn an Attention Neural Network into an Interpretable Hard-Logic Predicate Circuit: Truth-Table Predicate Extraction and State-Machine Merging under Ship-of-Theseus Replacement
papers.abstract: We convert a trained attention network as a whole, attention included, into a hard-logic predicate circuit that runs in its place. Every unit of the circuit is a 0/1 predicate on tokens, and every map between predicates is a minimised truth table. Short tables, such as the product of a query code and a key code, are minimised exactly, and wide feature-to-feature transitions become implication rules by noise-tolerant minimisation. Blocks are replaced one at a time from the output down, in the manner of the Ship of Theseus, and after each replacement the remaining soft part re-adapts to the frozen circuit. Attention selection takes two forms, a row-wise comparison of integer scores (order selection) and a learned rule (rule selection). Both are fitted on the ordinary training set alone, and only on the examples that the teacher classifies correctly, so that the circuit imitates the teacher where the teacher is right. On TweetEval-emotion, the complete circuit of DistilGPT2 reaches a test gold accuracy of 66.5 $\pm$ 1.3% with order selection and 57.4 $\pm$ 2.5% with rule selection over three seeds, against 74.7% for the teacher and 64.0% for a bag of word pieces fitted on the same tweets, and that of BERT-base reaches 70.0 $\pm$ 0.5% with order selection and 63.7 $\pm$ 1.2% with rule selection against 77.8%. The circuit needs no multiplier and no weight traffic, and its exported hardware description reproduces it bit for bit. By a synthesis-based estimate it classifies one tweet in about 1-2 $μ$s (DistilGPT2) and 3-5 $μ$s (BERT) on an FPGA card and in 5-9 $μ$s on a palm-sized board whose module draws 7.5-15 W, two to three orders of magnitude faster than the network on a GPU at batch 1 (measured, 0.9-2.6 ms for DistilGPT2 including an optimised CUDA-graph baseline), at a cost of 8.5 (DistilGPT2) and 8.6 (BERT) points of gold accuracy for the synthesised seed-0 circuits.

papers.title: Where Should a Diffusion Transformer Meet Its Teacher?
papers.abstract: Representation Alignment (REPA) significantly accelerates Diffusion Transformer training by guiding intermediate student features with a pretrained visual teacher, yet existing methods typically attach supervision to a single fixed layer. As student representations evolve, however, we find that the most effective layer for alignment varies across training stages. To track this evolving layer suitability online without costly search, we measure gradient compatibility between the flow-matching and alignment objectives, and propose AdaREPA, an online routing framework that adaptively selects the supervision layer as training progresses. AdaREPA uses a softmax distribution over smoothed layer compatibility scores to sample a layer for alignment at each training step. This probabilistic routing adapts teacher supervision to the student's changing learning needs, with minimal training overhead and no additional inference cost. On ImageNet-256, AdaREPA accelerates convergence and improves generation quality across model sizes, while revealing how the most suitable layers for supervision shift over training.

papers.title: MoE-Context: Show the Model Only What It Needs
papers.abstract: AI agents read their whole history at every step. People do not work like that: we keep what the moment needs and hold the rest as a rough note we can recall. MoE-Context applies this to language models. The context is split into blocks. Before each step a fast yes or no pass decides which blocks the step needs; the rest stay as one-line notes that can be brought back, and nothing is deleted. In the version we build, one model makes this decision and then answers, over a single key-value cache where hidden blocks are masked rather than removed. On a laptop with Qwen3-1.7B and a synthetic lookup task, showing only the needed block raises accuracy from 93 to 119 of 120, and a masked block is as hidden as a deleted one. The model's own picking is the weak part. A supervised linear probe written into spare output rows lifts its accuracy from 80 to 110 of 120, but simple keyword search picks perfectly on this task, and the probe does not transfer to a second task. We report these results openly, along with two cheap usage patterns that block switching enables: undoing a failed attempt and running subagents without a new context.

papers.title: Energy decay and asymptotic profile for a system of damped wave equations
papers.abstract: We consider a system of two wave or Klein-Gordon equations on the Euclidean space. One is damped, while the second is only indirectly damped via a coupling term. We are interested in the large time behavior of the solutions. More precisely, we prove energy decay for both components and, when possible, we give their asymptotic profiles. Our proofs are based on spectral analysis. We will see that in our setting the contribution of high frequencies always decays exponentially, so the results depend on the contribution of low frequencies. We observe a diffusive phenomenon as for a single wave equation, but the coupling between the two components gives completely different behaviors, depending on the nature of the equations and the strengths of the damping and coupling.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization: Fusing Expert Knowledge with Numerical Data
papers.abstract: Multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (MFBO) reduces engineering design cost by combining inexpensive low-fidelity (LF) models with a few accurate high-fidelity (HF) evaluations and sequentially selecting designs to evaluate. However, when HF data are scarce, the LF-HF discrepancy is difficult to learn from numerical data alone, especially when physics omitted in the LF model makes it design-dependent. Yet even without sufficient data, domain experts often know which physics the LF model omits and under which conditions its effect grows. Existing multi-fidelity (MF) models cannot use such qualitative knowledge directly, but large language models (LLMs) can interpret it and compare designs accordingly. The proposed LLM-Assisted MFBO adds a knowledge basis to the conventional MF model: from an expert description of the omitted physics, an LLM judges which of two designs requires the larger signed residual correction, and a pairwise Gaussian process converts these judgments into the basis. HF data calibrate its contribution and sign, so the knowledge is not trusted blindly. On a lithium-ion battery design problem, the proposed method reduced the regret area under the curve of conventional MFBO by 61%. Knowledge quality, rather than the choice of LLM, determined whether the search was accelerated, as shown by a controlled study that varied the two independently. A knowledge-level ablation further quantified the contribution of each knowledge statement. These results show that LLM-interpreted expert knowledge can complement numerical data as an information source in MFBO.

papers.title: Teaching VLMs What to Say, Not How to Reason: Rethinking Counterfactual Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving systems have been shown to suffer from shortcut learning and causal confusion, limiting their ability to generalize robustly under distribution shift. To mitigate these limitations, recent works based on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have explored incorporating linguistic reasoning capabilities into driving decision-making, reporting improvements in driving performance. In particular, counterfactual (CF) reasoning has been proposed to enable self-reflective, high-level causal understanding. However, it remains unclear whether the language-based reasoning mitigates shortcut learning or merely shifts it from visual representations to linguistic patterns, creating an illusion of causal understanding. Moreover, existing approaches often conflate intervention-based reasoning with CF reasoning, leaving the effects of genuine CF reasoning unexplored. In this work, we examine what CF reasoning actually induces in VLM-based autonomous driving and observe that it shifts the action distribution toward more conservative behaviors while increasing uncertainty in reasoning and decision-making. This effect persists under reinforcement fine-tuning, suggesting that it is not merely a transient artifact. Furthermore, visual attention analysis shows that CF reasoning does not alter visual grounding, while causal intervention experiments reveal that masking causally relevant and non-causal factors in accident scenarios results in comparable decision change rates. Overall, these results suggest that CF reasoning does not induce genuine causal reasoning grounded in visual evidence. Instead, it acts as a linguistic shortcut that reshapes the action distribution, teaching models what to say but not how to reason, highlighting a gap between language-based reasoning and causal understanding in autonomous driving.

papers.title: SearchDiffusion: Information-Guided Diffusion Planning for Object Search
papers.abstract: Object search in unknown environments requires robots to gather useful observations while avoiding obstacles and accounting for limited sensor visibility. We present SearchDiffusion, a diffusion-based planner that generates position and heading trajectories using a learned dense utility map. The map represents geometric accessibility, useful visibility, and semantic progress. It conditions trajectory generation and provides an objective for sampling guidance. Sampled map hypotheses provide additional geometric context, while geometric and heading guidance, validity checks, and analytical selection support execution. Across 90 simulated tasks on 24 map layouts, SearchDiffusion achieved 95.6\% target detection at greater computational cost. Ablations show complementary benefits from utility and guidance, with limited additional detection benefit from runtime map hypotheses. In ten physical quadruped trials using OneMap relevance maps, eight were successful under operator assessment, without fine-tuning on real-robot data. These results support combining learned spatial utility with guided trajectory generation for object search under partial observability.

papers.title: Interpretable uncertainties for bounds on spectral functionals from Euclidean correlators
papers.abstract: Positivity of the spectral density, combined with a $χ^2$ measure of compatibility with the data, bounds every linear functional of the spectral density of a Euclidean correlator to an interval. We show how such an interval is turned into a central value with statistical and systematic errors that have a definite meaning. We first show that, at typical precision, the best positive fit of noisy data has $χ^2_{\min}>0$, with a probability bounded from below by the distance of the noise-free data from the boundary of the set of data of positive spectra. Numerically, it does not depend on the number of states. The threshold must therefore be set relative to $χ^2_{\min}$. With $Δχ^2=1$, the interval reproduces Gaussian error propagation when positivity does not act, and positivity can only narrow it. We define the statistical error by the jackknife and the systematic error as the remaining, non-Gaussian part of the interval, which becomes a systematic error that does not decrease with the statistics in the high-statistics limit. Coverage tests for correlators and for smeared spectral densities and step functions give nominal coverage for outputs determined by the data and mostly conservative coverage otherwise. The exceptions are effects of the statistical error on the error estimate that disappear as the statistics is increased. Additional bounds on the spectral density, for example from perturbation theory, further reduce the systematic error substantially without loss of coverage. For long-distance correlators the method uses the same information as the bounding method, and its error agrees with that of the bounding method up to the remaining gap between the bounds.

papers.title: CanopyKV: Remember beyond the Crop for Fast Active Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract: Active visual reasoning enables multimodal models to answer challenging visual questions by gathering fine-grained evidence through iterative image inspection and tool use. However, accumulating crops and reasoning tokens expands the key-value (KV) cache, making compression important for reducing memory and inference costs. Existing KV compression methods typically select historical tokens based on attention, recency, or redundancy. These criteria do not explicitly distinguish locally replaced evidence from complementary information needed for future exploration: each crop refreshes a local region, while earlier views may still support subsequent decisions. Discarding such evidence can impair accuracy or require additional search, while scoring and cache reorganization can offset the computational savings from compression. We introduce CanopyKV, a training-free KV compression framework that uses parent-child crop relationships to retain complementary evidence, keeps retained history stable, and protects the state needed for ongoing reasoning. Tool metadata provides retention signals without additional attention scoring, while compact KV storage reduces subsequent attention costs. Across VisualProbe, V*, HR-Bench, and MME-Lite, CanopyKV achieves state-of-the-art answer accuracy and end-to-end efficiency among the evaluated KV compression methods. On MME-Lite, it retains approximately one-quarter of Dense's total KV while improving accuracy by 10.5 percentage points and accelerating complete reasoning by $1.64\times$.

papers.title: No room for $X(2370)$ exceptionalism: the glueball interpretation warrants caution
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/ψ$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/ψ\toγPPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0η^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $η(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $η_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/ψ\toγπ^0π^0η$ and $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

papers.title: One Affinity, Two Axes: Bidirectional Slot Attention for Iterative Aggregation across the Structure--Detail Spectrum in Visual Retrieval
papers.abstract: Aggregating dense patch tokens into compact and discriminative global descriptors is central to visual retrieval. Although foundation models provide rich local features, existing aggregation heads still rely on single-pass mappings and lack an explicit mechanism to coordinate structural and fine-grained cues. Therefore, we propose Bidirectional Slot Attention (BiSA), which reformulates aggregation as an iterative coupled system. Cross-Axis Consensus (CAC) progressively refines learnable slots by interpreting a single shared token--slot affinity along two complementary axes. Along the competition axis, slots vie for each token under a temperature shared across all of them, determining token ownership and inducing a non-redundant scene decomposition. Along the selection axis, a slot-specific temperature governs the breadth of each slot's response, spanning a spectrum from broad layouts to sparse fine-grained details. Their consensus couples non-redundant decomposition with multi-granular slot specialization. Furthermore, the two axes expose intrinsic token-reliability cues at no extra cost: a token's claim strength under competition and its salience under selection. Progressive Token Filtering (PTF) converts these cues into a retention probability that down-weights unreliable tokens before the next CAC iteration, without any segmentation branch or external prior, forming a self-reinforcing loop of competitive decomposition, selective focusing, and feedback purification. Across all three retrieval tasks, BiSA leads on five of six place recognition benchmarks (+4.2 R@1 on Baidu Mall), tops all 16 metrics of drone--satellite geo-localization (+8.4 R@1 at 150 m), and improves instance-level retrieval on ROxford-Hard by 4.5 mAP points. Notably, the selection axis adds only 20 learnable scalars, yet improves average R@1 by 2.8 points.

papers.title: Geodesic-informed neural networks for testing spacetimes with S2
papers.abstract: Stellar orbits around Sagittarius A*, in particular that of S2, test the spacetime of the Galactic Center. Such analyses usually integrate the equations of motion for every likelihood evaluation and sample the posterior. We develop a differentiable orbit model for static, spherically symmetric spacetimes that obtains the parameters, their uncertainties and the Bayesian evidence by optimization rather than sampling. In the Geodesic-Informed Neural Network (GINN), the conserved quantities, the shape of the orbit and the redshift are computed exactly from the metric, and a neural network constrained by the geodesic equation represents the time evolution of the radial phase. The physical parameters and the network weights minimize a single loss with Adam and Gauss-Newton steps, and the curvature at the minimum gives the uncertainties and the evidence. We test this Gaussian approximation against a second-order expansion and an exact geodesic solver, and apply GINN to the S2 data in the Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordström, hairy Horndeski, Bardeen, Janis-Newman-Winicour and Yukawa spacetimes. GINN reproduces the estimates and uncertainties of the exact solver. For Schwarzschild we find $M=(4.32\pm0.22)\times10^6\,M_\odot$ and $D=8.33\pm0.21$ kpc. No spacetime deviates significantly from Schwarzschild; a Yukawa correction, for example, is limited to $|δ|<0.011$ (95%) at a range of about 180 AU. No additional parameter improves the fit enough to pay its Occam penalty, so the Bayes factors range from inconclusive to moderate in favor of Schwarzschild. The Gaussian approximation is accurate when the hair enters the metric linearly and conservative when it enters only through its square. When the posterior is close to Gaussian, GINN gives the estimates, their uncertainties and the evidence from a single optimization, and the same derivatives quantify departures from it.

papers.title: Doppler effect on dual-downlink time-bin quantum key distribution and a proposed ephemeris-assisted witness-field correction
papers.abstract: Time-bin entanglement is promising for satellite Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) due to its compatibility with telecom fiber networks, but its phase-sensitive measurements are vulnerable to Doppler effects induced by satellite motion. We present a spectral-temporal framework for time-bin-entangled photon pairs generated onboard a satellite via Spontaneous Parametric Down Conversion (SPDC) and distributed to two Optical Ground Stations (OGSs) over independent downlinks with distinct Doppler shifts. Each OGS is equipped with an Unbalanced Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (UMZI) used to perform Bennett-Brassard-Mermin 1992 (BBM92) entangled-photon QKD. In a simulated Low Earth Orbit (LEO) pass with matched 400 ps analyzer delays, the received time-bin separation changes by at most 8.8 fs per link, while the combined carrier phase shifts by about 38 rad, which primarily degrades phase-basis correlations. After zero-Doppler calibration, this phase separates into independent signal-and idler-link contributions, allowing each station to correct its link Doppler phase shift locally, without real-time phase exchange between the stations. We propose an ephemeris-assisted feed-forward architecture, in which an auxiliary interferometer analyzes a co-propagating classical witness field to reconstruct the local Doppler-induced phase, which a phase modulator then compensates on the quantum channel. In a noise-free model, a 1 Hz sample-and-hold correction rate keeps the phase-basis Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) below 2% and retains 93% of the ideal asymptotic key yield. After 18 accumulated passes, the corrected finite secret key reaches 95% of its ideal length, whereas relabeling the parity from the ephemeris without optical correction reaches only about 8%.

papers.title: Hadronic production of excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC
papers.abstract: We study the hadronic production of ground-state and excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC for $\sqrt{S}=13$ TeV within the framework of NRQCD factorization at leading order in QCD. The calculation includes the $1S$, $1P$, and $2S$ multiplets, with both color-singlet and color-octet contributions to direct $1P$ production. For $p_T>0.2$ GeV, the summed production cross section is $336.04^{+275.80}_{-175.43}$ nb; the quoted uncertainty combines the specified heavy-quark mass and common-scale variations and does not include PDF-set differences. The NNPDF3.0 and MSHT20LO predictions are approximately $23\%$--$24\%$ below the CT18LO result. With the adopted radiative-transition branching fractions, $2S$ feed-down increases the total $1P$ yield from $34.73$ to $75.34$ nb. The relative enhancement differs markedly among the four spectroscopic states, ranging from $38\%$ for $1^1P_1$ to $262\%$ for $1^3P_0$, and it reorders their integrated production hierarchy. Within the set of states included here, the ratio of the $1P$ yield to the inclusive ground-state yield increases from $0.103$ to $0.224$. We present the state-resolved distributions and the dependence of direct production on kinematic cuts, parton distributions, quark masses, and scale choices. These results illustrate the potential impact of $2S$ feed-down on the relative yields of the lowest $P$-wave $B_c$ states.

papers.title: VAFL: A Vertical Analytic Federated Learning Mechanism for Efficient Crowdsourced Services via Closed-Form Solutions
papers.abstract: Intelligent services often rely on complementary information held by different organizations, motivating Vertical Federated Learning without centralized raw-data pooling. We propose VAFL, a Vertical Analytic Federated Learning framework that fits classification and regression heads on fixed local representations through regularized least squares. An agent-assisted protected-computation workflow supports two-party and multi-party collaboration. To reduce fitting overhead, we develop a full-dimensional equivalent solve that applies block factors directly to the target matrix, avoiding construction of the full inverse. We further study two width-reduction strategies: local spectral projection with coefficient lifting, and full-dimensional local fitting with low-rank cross-party correction. The first compresses the prediction space, whereas the second retains local components outside the collaboration subspace. We establish their algebraic properties and analyze their computational scope. Experiments on five benchmarks show the accuracy--cost tradeoffs of these strategies and compatibility with diverse frozen backbones. Predictive performance and training time identify useful operating points and the limits of compression.

papers.title: SCOUT: Risk-Guided Foundation-Model Escalation for Robust Tissue Detection in Whole-Slide Images
papers.abstract: Reliable tissue detection is essential for whole-slide image analysis, yet high average segmentation accuracy can conceal failures involving pale tissue, small fragments, and heterogeneous staining. Pathology foundation models offer transferable representations, but exhaustive inference is computationally demanding and may introduce false-positive tissue predictions. We propose SCOUT (Selective Correction of Uncertain Tissue), a risk-guided cascade that selectively refines an initial thumbnail-based tissue mask. A lightweight audit network estimates the spatial distribution of segmentation errors and prioritizes candidate regions for processing by a frozen pathology foundation model. An asymmetric consensus rule integrates the resulting predictions with the initial mask to recover missed tissue while limiting false positives. A calibrated slide-level review score additionally controls the marginal rate of unflagged case-group failures under the calibration assumptions. Evaluation on a public multi-source, multi-stain benchmark shows that SCOUT reduces the proportion of case groups requiring mask correction from 38.1% for the best released detector to 18.6%, with particularly pronounced improvements in immunohistochemistry. Source-held-out experiments demonstrate better generalization than a segmentation network trained on the same annotations, while selective inference achieves an observed failure rate no higher than processing all candidate regions. Downstream, lymph-node classification with SCOUT masks is non-inferior to that obtained with two of the three released detectors evaluated. A variant built on an openly licensed foundation model is publicly released as an installable Python package with trained weights. These results support risk-guided foundation-model inference as an effective approach to tissue detection across heterogeneous histopathology data.

papers.title: Lelong Numbers Above an Arbitrary Bound and Plane Curves
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a positive closed current of bidimension $(1,1)$ with unit mass on $\mathbb P^2$ and $E^+_α(T)$ be the upper level sets of Lelong numbers $ν(T,x)$ of $T$. For any $α\geq \frac{3}{d+5}$, $d\in \mathbb Z^+$ we show that $|E^+_α(T)\setminus C|\leq 2$ for a curve $C$ of degree $d$. As a corollary of this result, we obtain a quantative lower bound for the integrability exponent at any point away from the curve $C$ and a two point set $P$.

papers.title: CHORUS: Cross-Subject Harmonization via Population Relay for Unseen Subjects in Brain Visual Decoding
papers.abstract: EEG-based image retrieval performs well on training subjects but generalizes poorly to unseen individuals. Existing calibration methods address this gap by aligning a new subject directly with image embeddings. We find that the training population is a better alignment target: an unseen subject's embeddings are closer to the stimulus-matched population average than to the image embeddings, and the remaining gap to the population is largely a shift and a rotation. Motivated by this finding, we propose CHORUS. At training, stimulus-matched cross-subject averaging (SCA) teaches the encoder to match responses to the same image across subjects; at deployment, a two-stage calibration first aligns an unseen subject to population anchors predicted from the decoder's visual features, and then to the image embeddings. On leave-one-subject-out THINGS-EEG2 with two backbones, CHORUS improves over direct calibration by 10.92 and 6.63 points on unlabeled test batches and by 4.2-6.9 points with 10-200 labeled pairs; even without the population stage, SCA and direct calibration each outperform prior training and calibration schemes. The complete system reaches 78.37% and 73.40% 200-way Top-1 accuracy, 36.32 and 20.93 points above SCORE.

papers.title: Transferable Named Sparse Features for Morphology-based Gleason Grading
papers.abstract: Deep learning systems grade prostate biopsies at the level of pathologists, but most report a grade without the glandular architecture that justifies it. This work presents a grading system built on a sparse code over the tokens of a pathology foundation model. A sparse autoencoder pretrained on biopsies is aligned with multi-reader annotations, so that 69 of its 2048 features are named after Gleason morphologies such as cribriform glands, cords, and comedonecrosis. The same code feeds a grading network, which reads all features to predict Gleason patterns and the Grade Group, while morphology maps read directly from the named features. We evaluate the system on five public datasets that include needle biopsies, tissue-microarray cores, multi-reader annotations, and three scanners. The morphology maps remain stable across alignment runs and, without retraining, detect cribriform glands in external biopsies (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.849) and pattern 5 in unseen cores when evaluated by up to six pathologists (AUROC 0.846 to 0.919). In an independent biopsy cohort, Grade Group agreement with three pathologists on Leica scans is close to their agreement with each other. Removing the named features reduces the corresponding Gleason pattern predictions by 49% to 98%, with effects larger than those from 20 activity-matched random feature removals. These results show that a shared sparse representation can support competitive Gleason grading while providing named morphological evidence that transfers across datasets and whose contribution to grading can be measured directly.

papers.title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents routinely interact with untrusted external data, exposing them to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks that hijack agents into executing attacker-chosen tasks. To uncover these vulnerabilities at scale, automated red-teaming methods often leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to generate attacks that achieve high attack success rates (ASR). Model developers use the attacks discovered during internal red-teaming to harden agents through adversarial training before deployment, a collaborative offensive-defensive process known in cybersecurity as purple-teaming. However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training. Specifically, we find that two state-of-the-art RL-based red-teaming methods, RL-Hammer and PISmith, suffer from mode collapse, repeatedly discovering similar attack strategies whose additional successes add no additional robustness improvements to adversarial training. To address this gap, we introduce PIPETTE, a unified prompt injection purple-teaming framework that effectively converts red-teaming discoveries into defender robustness improvements. PIPETTE employs a dictionary learning-based reward that encourages broader coverage of attack strategies during red-teaming. It also integrates an on-policy adversarial training pipeline tailored to IPI defense, enabling agents to resist attacks while completing legitimate user tasks. Extensive evaluations across agentic benchmarks (AgentDojo and ASB) demonstrate that PIPETTE produces defenders that achieve near-zero attack success rates on static attacks and can withstand strong adaptive attacks, while maintaining benign task utility close to that of the undefended baseline.

papers.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

papers.title: Towards Pose-Robust Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning a vision-language-action (VLA) model on a few dozen demonstrations is the standard way to put a manipulation policy on a robot, yet the resulting policy silently assumes that the camera and the robot base stay exactly where they were during data collection: a bumped tripod or a base re-docked a few centimetres away makes it reach for the wrong place. We show that both failures are one phenomenon, a change of the camera-to-base extrinsic that the policy has memorised, and that the robot carries everything needed to undo it. We introduce WACO, a world-anchored canonicalization framework for VLA models: the arm, placed by forward kinematics at the measured joint angles, serves as a metric calibration target, and the static scene serves as the world anchor that tells a moved camera from a moved robot. From a single RGB-D frame, WACO estimates both shifts without ground-truth extrinsics or extra data, canonicalises the image to the calibration viewpoint and the state, action and start pose to the calibration base frame, and fine-tunes the unmodified policy under the artefacts of its own estimator. We also introduce LIBERO-PoseShift, the first benchmark for RGB VLAs with graded camera, base and compound shifts. Across LIBERO-PoseShift, the LIBERO-Plus camera track and four real-world tasks on a UR5e robot, WACO consistently outperforms the standard few-shot recipe and prior viewpoint-robust methods, raising shifted success by 13.2 points in simulation and by 36.7 points on the real robot, recovering 90% of the simulation gap to a ground-truth oracle and 87% of the real-robot gap, and establishing a new state of the art among methods that use no perturbed training data, with no test-time calibration. Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/WACO/.

papers.title: Isometrically greedy renormings of bidemocratic unconditional bases of Banach spaces
papers.abstract: We show that if a greedy basis of a Banach space has the additional property that its dual basis is also greedy, then the space admits an equivalent norm under which the basis is isometrically greedy. This solves in the positive a question posed by Dilworth, Kutzarova, Odell, Schlumprecht and Zsák in 2014. As an application, we resolve a long-standing problem explicitly posed by Albiac, Ansorena and Wallis in 2017 by proving that any subsymmetric basis of a Banach space is isometrically greedy under a suitable renorming of the ambient space.

papers.title: Spontaneous emission of atomic systems near metallic and semiconducting atomic chains
papers.abstract: We investigate the spontaneous emission of a quantum emitter placed near finite atomic chains described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By tuning the chain from a metallic to a semiconducting character through dimerization, we analyze how the electronic structure of an atomic-scale scatterer, together with the illumination profile, determines the strength, bandwidth, and spatial structure of the spontaneous emission enhancement. The resonant enhancement depends on both spectral matching and the emitter position relative to the induced charge and field patterns. In metallic chains, the nearly harmonic energy spectrum leads to overlapping optical transitions and strong resonances. For semiconducting chains, dimerization opens a gap and leads to a modified density of electronic states, redistributing the response over a broader spectral range and reducing its peak intensity. Coulomb interactions affect the optical resonances through blueshift or modification of their spatial character, and act differently on collective and single-particle-like excitations. Finally, we show that the same mechanisms demonstrated in atomic chains persist in realistic quasi-one-dimensional systems, including trans-polyacetylene chains and graphene nanoribbons. Our findings indicate a general direction for engineering light-matter interactions at the atomic scale, and may offer design principles for tunable nanoscale photonic and quantum-optical devices.

papers.title: Semantic Context Handoff with On-Demand Evidence for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Traditional long-horizon LLM agents often hand off context through full-history prompting, retaining all previous action--observation interactions. As execution proceeds, this history keeps growing, increasing inference cost and potentially degrading accuracy. Existing methods control this growth by preserving compact conclusions while removing earlier observations, but doing so can discard evidence that later becomes relevant. We introduce Semantic Context Handoff (SCH), whose central abstraction is state--evidence separation: a compact semantic state carries the agent's current interpretation, while supporting action--observation evidence remains separately addressable and can re-enter context when later execution makes it relevant, without separate summarization or retrieval-model calls. Empirically, SCH improves long-horizon agent performance while substantially reducing context cost. In a controlled 150-task SWE-bench study, SCH's evidence recovery improves Pass@1 from $80.0\%$ to $86.9\%$ at essentially unchanged token use and execution time. In the complete-system comparison, SCH achieves 86.9% Pass@1 while using 43% fewer tokens and 41% less wall-clock time than the strongest baseline by task performance. Across models and benchmarks, SCH consistently reduces token use relative to full-history prompting while remaining competitive with or improving upon the evaluated baselines. Trajectory analysis confirms that SCH recovers evidence from substantially earlier parts of the interaction history rather than merely preserving a recent context window.

papers.title: Sharp Sobolev thresholds and rapid rotation for Navier--Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with fractional horizontal dissipation $νΛ_h^{2α}$, $0<α\le1$, and a Coriolis force. There is no vertical dissipation. The scaling-critical Sobolev index is $s_c=5/2-2α$. For $0<α<1$, we prove local Hadamard well-posedness in $H^s$ for $s\ge s_c$; for $α=1$, the range is $s>1/2$. At every prescribed finite rotation rate, norm inflation holds in all remaining positive-order Sobolev spaces for classical solutions with smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, starting from arbitrarily small $H^s$ data in arbitrarily short time. Thus $H^{s_c}$ is a well-posedness space for $0<α<1$, whereas $H^{1/2}$ exhibits norm inflation for $α=1$. These results give sharp Sobolev thresholds for each finite rotation rate. Throughout the well-posedness range, small data yield global solutions with a rotation-independent smallness threshold, and every fixed datum yields a global solution for sufficiently rapid rotation. The nonlinear solution converges to the linear Stokes--Coriolis evolution uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ and in the global dissipation norm as $|Ω|\to\infty$. For spectrally localized data separated from the vertical frequency axis, the convergence rate is $O(|Ω|^{-γ})$ for every $0<γ<1/2$. For $0<α<1$, the energy estimates close at $s=s_c$ without loss of derivatives in isotropic Sobolev spaces, using Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Sobolev trace inequalities, and localized horizontal product estimates. Below $s_c$, norm inflation follows from an approximation by a fixed smooth Euler solution after rescaling. At $(α,s)=(1,1/2)$, viscosity remains fixed under critical rescaling; the construction instead uses a localized scalar shear and conormal analytic stability estimates uniform in the vertical concentration parameters.

papers.title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Residual-based methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), physics-informed Kolmogorov--Arnold networks, and some physics-informed neural operator architectures, approximate PDE solutions by minimizing a discrete least-squares loss formed from the PDE and boundary residuals over a prescribed trial class. This structure is shared by classical least-squares Kansa collocation, whose kernel trial spaces admit an established convergence theory. For neural trial classes, approximation power alone does not ensure that discrete residuals control the continuous solution error. For linear elliptic Dirichlet problems, we extend the kernel-based collocation framework to neural trial classes through elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency. Elliptic regularity supplies the PDE estimate relating solution error to continuous residuals. Discrete stability identifies admissible trial subclasses in which continuous residuals are controlled by a computable discrete loss. This step also quantifies the required number of collocation points. Furthermore, the stability analysis naturally demands a scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weight. For the constrained problem, consistency requires accurate comparison functions within the same admissible subclass, a requirement not supplied by neural approximation estimates alone. Specializing to multilayer perceptrons with tanh activations (tanh-MLPs), we construct admissible comparison networks and establish convergence for the constrained residual minimization problem. We further obtain conditional convergence of unconstrained physics-balanced PINNs based on tanh-MLPs under joint network and sampling refinement.

papers.title: Curvature Gradients Turn Shear into Superflow in Supersolids
papers.abstract: Supersolids on curved surfaces are becoming experimentally accessible. We develop a Galilean-covariant effective field theory of supersolids on curved surfaces and show that gradients of Gaussian curvature couple lattice shear to compression with a strength fixed by the shear modulus and the curvature gradient. As a result, shear drives superflow. On spheroids this yields geometric selection rules and multiplet splittings; near mode crossings, weak deformations produce hybrids in which superfluid and lattice carry comparable kinetic energy, and shear becomes visible as a density response.

papers.title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
papers.abstract: Scientific figures carry evidence for the claims that cite them, so reviewing a paper means checking that a figure agrees with the text, and not only describing what the figure shows.
