Our analysis works by bounding the statistical variance of the adversary's posterior likelihood of where a message of interest is at a given point in time. Using concentration bounds on this distribution, we show that parallel mixnets satisfy $(\varepsilon, δ)$-differential indistinguishability for messages routed through the mixnet (similar to $(\varepsilon, δ)$-differential privacy) with very small failure probabilities $δ$ and small privacy parameters $\varepsilon$ under reasonable operating conditions. Our model also enables an examination of the quantitative trade-off between anonymity, latency and per-router bandwidth in parallel mixnets.

papers.title: The additive ambiguity of gravitational entropy fixed by the topology of the horizon
papers.abstract: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant. In this work we argue that in four-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity this constant is the Gauss--Bonnet contribution to the Wald entropy, and that it is carried by the normalization of the trace and not by the state. In particular, the conical expansion of the Gauss--Bonnet density is exactly linear in the deficit angle, and on smooth squashed cones it reduces to the intrinsic curvature of the cut, so that the term is a constant on every smooth cross-section and carries no boost energy. Its Noether charge is invariant under all deformations within a topological sector and central in any algebra that preserves the sector, and thus a state-independent constant on such an algebra can only rescale the trace. Additionally, when the boundary of the subregion is completed as the Euler action requires, the Gauss--Bonnet term does not contribute to the presymplectic form, the crossed product is inherited from Einstein gravity, and the constant is the Euler number of the excised Euclidean tip. We state the hypotheses, we weaken factoriality to a central decomposition, and we illustrate the mechanism in Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity and in topological black holes in anti-de Sitter space, where the topological weight displaces the Hawking--Page temperature and a black-hole merger shifts the coarse-grained boundary entropy by a state-independent amount.

papers.title: Covariate-Indexed Inclusion Probabilities on Unbalanced Panels
papers.abstract: We estimate the probability that an item with given covariates belongs to a set when the cross-section changes over time and items and periods are dependent. We propose two convex models whose fitted probabilities are nonnegative by construction and remain valid whatever the dependence between items, for which we establish consistency, finite-sample bounds and limit distributions for serially dependent panels. One suits events of moderate or high probability, the other rare events, and half the disagreement between their fits estimates a lower bound on the misspecification error of the worse fit, without knowledge of the true probabilities. On monthly US stock failures, the rare-event model predicts better than the ordinary logit and the classical failure logit. With the eight classical predictors, most of the gain comes from basis functions of the rank angle of each predictor and summary.

papers.title: Optical rectification and Pockels effect in the organic nonlinear crystal MBI for quasi-discrete THz time-domain spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Organic nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals offer efficient nonlinear frequency conversion for broadband THz spectroscopy. Unfortunately, only a subset of NLO crystals is compatible with the telecom (~1.5 $μ$m) pump wavelength region, where convenient MHz-rate femtosecond fiber lasers are available. Here, we present ultra-broadband (1-30 THz) THz generation and detection using a benzoindolium iodide (MBI, C$_{24}$H$_{24}$NOI) crystal illuminated by a 1.5 $μ$m MHz-rate fiber laser. At 200 mW of average pump power, the crystal delivers ~1 $μ$W of THz radiation as quasi-discrete peaks covering the whole emission region with a prominent peak at 11.8 THz. High-dynamic range (>40 dB) time-domain spectroscopy is demonstrated within minutes of integration.

papers.title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped vision-language models (VLMs) deepen computation by reusing shared layers, approaching larger models' capabilities with fewer parameters and easing the storage and deployment burden of stacking independent layers. However, repeatedly processing long visual sequences still incurs substantial compute and GPU memory costs. Visual token compression reduces these costs by shortening sequences. Existing methods mainly select original tokens directly or combine selection with aggregation. In looped models, the former may overlook changing token importance across calls and discard information needed later; the latter lack joint consideration of output changes across calls, limiting information preservation. We propose LoopZip, a training-free visual token compression algorithm addressing both issues. Visual aggregation builds a compact candidate pool before the looped backbone, and cross-invocation selection averages instruction attention from the first two existing calls of the same shared attention layer to retain tokens needed by both states. Weight-tied value correction then jointly fits shared visual-value adjustments to both pre-selection layer outputs, reducing output deviations across states. To validate LoopZip's effectiveness, we conduct extensive experiments covering two open-source looped VLMs, eleven benchmarks, and three pruning ratios. On LoopVL-1B, LoopZip retains 97.16% of the original model's performance at 50% pruning ratio and exceeds the strongest baseline by 5.36% at 87.5% pruning ratio. Across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang, LoopVL-1B with LoopZip reduces peak allocated GPU memory by 58.36%-58.98% and achieves 2.01-2.47x end-to-end speedups over the original model.

papers.title: SlopeGuard: Towards Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection via Radial Spectral Slope Guidance
papers.abstract: AI-generated image detectors often overfit to generator-specific artifacts, hindering generalization to unseen synthesis pipelines. Existing frequency-based methods usually learn high-dimensional spectral patterns that may preserve generator-dependent variations. We explore Radial Spectral Slope, a compact descriptor of global spectral decay that captures transferable spectral trends while suppressing fine-grained variations. Our analysis shows that real and generated images exhibit systematic but generator-dependent slope differences, indicating that slope provides useful forensic evidence but is insufficient as a standalone decision criterion. This motivates combining spectral slope with semantic representations for more robust detection. Based on this insight, we propose SlopeGuard, which couples slope-aware data processing with slope guided feature learning to construct informative patch-based views, integrate Radial Spectral Slope with semantic features, and adapt prior preservation according to spectral atypicality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SlopeGuard achieves state-of-the-art mean accuracies of 97.5% on AIGCDetectBench, 97.8% on GenImage, and 85.1% on AIGIBench, while maintaining competitive performance under blur, cropping, JPEG compression, and additive noise.

papers.title: Stress Testing a Multimodal Large Language Model Grading Assistant on Kinematics Graph Reading
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can recognize graph features yet award credit without sufficient graphical support. This exploratory study examines selected grading outputs for synthetic responses to four kinematics exercises, generated through visual distortion and progressive transformation toward reference graphs. Different model and prompt configurations were used. Some judgments correctly distinguished instantaneous zero velocity from rest over a finite interval and recognized positive curvature. Yet a severely distorted velocity--time graph received full credit despite disconnected and branching traces and an unclear zero-velocity reference. Other submissions graded under the same configuration lost substantial credit. Numerical cutoffs intended to distinguish meaningful features from drawing irregularities were supplied without a coordinate convention for unnumbered graphs, leaving the basis of exact partial-credit awards unresolved. Stress testing can expose unsupported awards before classroom use. For the configurations examined, we do not recommend accepting scores as final grades without instructor review, including review of full-credit responses.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves Population Study for Testing Kerr Hypothesis: Are Non-Kerr Deformations Universal or Source-Dependent?
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of binary black hole mergers can test the Kerr black hole hypothesis in the strong-field and dynamical regime. In our previous works, we constrained the deformation parameters $α_{13}$ and $ε_3$ of the Johannsen metric using individual inspiral-dominated events from GWTC-3 and GWTC-4 and found no evidence of deviations from the Kerr solution. Here we combine 17 of these events to test whether black holes are Kerr, share a common non-zero deformation, or have deformations that vary from source to source. We first estimate the Savage--Dickey Bayes factor of each event, and we test how it depends on the prior range and on the removal of single events. We then combine the event likelihoods assuming a universal deformation, yielding a tighter joint constraint. Next, we perform a simple hierarchical analysis by assuming that the event-level deformation parameters are drawn from a population with mean $μ$ and intrinsic scatter $σ$. A universal deformation is constrained to $α_{13}=-0.01^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $ε_3=0.06^{+0.59}_{-0.54}$. The means from the population are consistent with zero for both parameters, and the scatter is not resolved by the current data. Our results are consistent with the Kerr hypothesis, but they cannot yet distinguish a shared deformation from a source-dependent one.

papers.title: ConserveEdit: Source-Anchored Transactions for Drift-Bounded Iterative Image Editing
papers.abstract: Instruction-driven image editors produce convincing local edits in one pass, but inside an iterative refinement loop every accepted output becomes the next input, so unintended changes outside the requested region accumulate. We present ConserveEdit, an editor-agnostic controller that treats each refinement step as a transaction against a contract compiled once from the source image. The contract separates what may change (the authorized region of each target, with a bounded halo for shadows and reflections) from what must survive (protected content with explicit tolerances). Candidates from a frozen editor are composed through a source-anchored mask and committed only if target progress, drift on protected content, and image quality pass as separate tests; otherwise the step is rolled back and repaired. For any editor, this keeps every pixel outside the authorized region bit-exact and bounds drift independently of the number of iterations, whereas no fixed scalar trade-off reproduces the separate tests. On all 1053 MagicBrush test edits with a frozen Qwen-Image-Edit, masking is necessary but not sufficient. A direct call already alters the rest of the image (12.1 dB PSNR outside the mask); composed through the source-anchored mask, it stays bit-exact there and its DINO similarity to the ground truth rises from 0.67 to 0.85, matching ConserveEdit, so this gain comes from the mask. Next to automatic masks, however, masked direct editing changes a protected face or text on 48% of turns, and masked scalar selection avoids this mostly by abstaining (23% constrained success). Because its drift test names the violated entity, ConserveEdit shrinks the support instead (2% violations, 53% constrained success); in a simulator with known ground truth it raises constrained success from 55.0% to 61.8%. Automatic grounding remains the main bottleneck. Code and logs will be released.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Analysis of CMS Open Data: Prompt J/psi Cross-Section Measurements in pp and Peripheral PbPb Collisions at sqrt(S)= 7 TeV and sqrt(sNN) = 2.76 TeV
papers.abstract: We investigate the use of an artificial-intelligence (AI) coding agent, supervised by human physicists, for collider physics analyses using CMS Open Data. OpenAI Codex performs dimuon event selection, two-dimensional invariant-mass and decay-length fits, Monte Carlo detector simulations, and systematic uncertainty evaluation after acquiring physics and experimental knowledge from published studies and external references, with human review at each stage. The workflow is tested on two CMS datasets, with custom full-detector simulations used to determine acceptance and reconstruction efficiencies. In proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV, prompt J/psi differential cross sections are measured versus transverse momentum and rapidity. The ratios of remeasured to published CMS cross sections have a mean of 1.000 and an RMS spread of 0.215 across 39 bins. In peripheral (50-100% centrality) PbPb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV, the corresponding prompt J/psi fiducial cross-section ratios have a mean of 1.158 and an RMS spread of 0.225 across six intervals. We identify agent failure modes and demonstrate the importance of structured human review in ensuring reliable results.

papers.title: Practice in Text, Act in Pixels: Correcting Where Perception Fails
papers.abstract: GUI agents can learn cheaply from a text view of an interface and act on screenshots through a vision-language screen reader. Yet on a simulated mobile platform with a low-cost reader, policies that complete most tasks in text fail on many of the same tasks on screenshots. We ask where a small budget of real screenshots is best spent to close this gap. We find that the reader's misreads are systematic and recur on the same interface elements. Noise matched to the reader's error rates, a natural sim-to-real remedy, misses this structure, and in a pre-specified comparison it did not beat training the policy directly on screenshots. We therefore correct the misreads at their source with reader alignment, which fine-tunes the reader on screenshots paired with their text views. The reader learns to output each screen's text view, as in text practice, and the policy stays unchanged. Spent on the reader, the screenshot budget gives 80.9% full-task success on new task instances, against 55.6% when spent on training the policy. Given the same labeled screenshots, adapting the reader also beats adapting the policy, and a single aligned reader improves every text-trained policy we tried without retraining any of them.

papers.title: HADVQ: Hessian Aware Directional Vector Quantization
papers.abstract: Ultra-low-bit quantization of large language models is a challenging task because aggressive compression severely distorts model parameters and disproportionately harms a small number of highly sensitive channels. We present a vector quantization method tailored for this regime. Our approach begins with random preconditioning, which regularizes the weight space and makes it more amenable to quantization. We then represent weights in polar coordinates and decouple the quantization of directions and magnitudes. To quantize directions, we leverage the structure induced by random preconditioning and design a structured codebook based on the $E_8$ lattice, yielding a compact yet expressive representation. To further reduce degradation, we detect extremely important channels using a proxy Hessian and preserve them with an additional cost of only 0.16 bits. Together, these components provide an effective quantization pipeline for LLMs in the extremely low-bit regime. Empirical results demonstrate improved accuracy, highlighting the benefit of combining geometric structure, lattice-based codebooks, and selective channel preservation.

papers.title: Positivity of Signed Odd-Multiplicity Partitions
papers.abstract: We establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for the signed partition $q$-series \[ A_k(q)= \sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k} \prod_{i=1}^k\frac{q^{j_i}}{1+q^{2j_i}} =\sum_{n\ge0}a_k(n)q^n, \qquad k\ge0, \] with $A_0(q)=1$. The coefficient $a_k(n)$ counts, with signs, partitions of $n$ having exactly $k$ distinct part sizes, each occurring with odd multiplicity. A partition with multiplicities $2t_1+1,\ldots,2t_k+1$ is assigned the sign $(-1)^{t_1+\cdots+t_k}$. We prove that $a_k(n)\ge0$ for all $k,n\ge0$, thereby resolving a conjecture on signed odd-multiplicity partitions. Our proof combines a positive theta--MacMahon factorization for the generating functions restricted to odd part sizes with a dyadic product decomposition that extends positivity to arbitrary part sizes. Moreover, we establish strict positivity $a_k(n)>0$ for every $k\ge2$ and $n\ge\binom{k+1}{2}$.

papers.title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $Ω_{gw}(f)/Ω_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.

papers.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
papers.abstract: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schrödinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless Pöschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.

papers.title: PCRG: Training-Free Pruning and Caching of Reference Tokens for Video Generation
papers.abstract: Reference-to-video diffusion transformers pack the variational autoencoder (VAE) latents of all references and the generated tokens into one full-attention sequence, in which reference tokens make up about half. Because attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length, these tokens take up an even larger share of the attention computation, yet most of them are static, smooth or irrelevant to the output. To accelerate reference-conditioned generation, we propose pruning and caching of reference tokens for video generation (PCRG), a training-free, plug-and-play method that uses two signals the model already computes to assign each reference token to one of three tiers, namely pruned, cached or kept. The first is a low-level redundancy r from VAE latents, since a token whose latent barely changes over time or across its neighbors adds little new content. The second is a high-level importance g from the vision-language-model (VLM) conditioner, where the attention that the prompt and any first or last frames pay to a token tells whether the output needs to read it. Tokens that are not redundant are kept, and redundant tokens are cached if important and pruned otherwise. Pruned tokens leave the sequence before the first step with all rotary position embedding positions unchanged. Cached tokens have their keys and values computed once and reused, and kept tokens are processed as usual. On MiniMax-H3, already distilled to 8 timesteps and quantized to int8, PCRG is 1.57x faster end to end on our V2V-Bench and 1.49x faster on the public VACE-Benchmark, while the quality of VBench drops by only 0.24% and 0.17%, respectively. PCRG shortens the sequence rather than changing how attention is computed or which steps are run, so it also stacks on step caching and sparse attention. On V2V-Bench it reaches 1.86x with TeaCache, 1.82x with Spark at nearly unchanged fidelity and 2.15x with Veda.

papers.title: High-Coverage Blind Spots in Online Abuse Monitoring: Account Selection, Held-Out Flagging Rates, and Sample Composition
papers.abstract: Platforms with limited monitoring capacity may rank target accounts by the number of abusive replies received or by the share of replies labeled abusive. We test how these rankings affect account selection, historical flagged-reply coverage, and held-out labeling rates. In the Online Abusive Attacks (OAA) data (945,987 replies to 384 accounts), two 25-account lists share just one account. Count-based selection covers 75.56% of flagged replies, while rate-based selection covers 5.04%. In a 500-iteration stratified historical hold-out, the lists have labeling rates of 2.69% and 4.98%, respectively (1.85 times). A volume- and group-preserving null model produces low list overlap without a corresponding rate advantage. We repeat the comparison on a second dataset of replies to UK election candidates. The two 25-account lists overlap in eight accounts, but the rate advantage is smaller in historical splits and reverses in three matched-group chronological tests. The findings distinguish differences in who is selected for monitoring from differences in future labeling rates across populations and time.

papers.title: TRAIL-IRL: Crossed Reward-Temperature Mixtures for Unlabeled Trajectory Clustering
papers.abstract: Different paths need not imply different preferences, trajectories also differ in how randomly actions are chosen. Many multi-reward inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) methods assume common action randomness and can confound it with preference heterogeneity. We introduce TRAIL-IRL, which clusters unlabeled trajectories using rewards for preferences and temperatures for action randomness. Its crossed mixture pairs each reward with a shared set of temperature levels, allowing action regularity to vary within preference groups. With centered and normalized rewards in a known finite-state environment, we establish the identifiability conditions under which the distribution of sufficiently long trajectories determines rewards, temperatures, mixing weights, and class counts up to relabeling. Under the same conditions and reward constraints, common-temperature reward mixtures with the same component count cannot reproduce a crossed mixture with multiple temperatures. We develop a generalized expectation-maximization algorithm and select class counts using the Bayesian information criterion (BIC). Simulations show improved predictive fit, reward recovery, and trajectory classification over common-temperature mixtures with the same component count. For 140 bird-year trajectories from 79 white storks, BIC favors four reward classes and three temperature levels over common-temperature candidates. Younger birds have higher posterior membership probabilities for a southwestward migration class, whereas older birds have higher probabilities for a northern retention class. Within reward classes, higher temperatures are associated with more variable movement directions and positions farther ahead along the migration route, consistent with social information use and collective sensing.

papers.title: Flexibility Has a Price: Quantifying Modality Policies in Maliciously Secure Multi-Biometric Authentication
papers.abstract: Multi-biometric authentication improves robustness and accessibility by combining information from multiple biometric modalities. Existing research has primarily focused on secure multimodal authentication, feature fusion, and recognition performance, while paying comparatively little attention to the security implications of modality-flexible authentication policies. At the same time, most systems provide limited cryptographic protection for biometric data during authentication. This paper addresses both challenges. We first study modality flexibility as a security decision rather than merely a usability feature. Each accepted modality subset creates an authentication entry point, and the resulting risk depends on the joint behavior of all accepted subsets and the attempt budget. We introduce a framework for quantifying this security cost and develop a policy-selection procedure that identifies policies satisfying a target risk level while supporting users who can present only a subset of modalities. We then present SUPERMBA, a two-server privacy-preserving authentication system that enforces the selected policy without revealing biometric templates or the modality subset used in an authentication attempt. The protocol provides verifiable policy enforcement even when one server is malicious and executes the same computation irrespective of the chosen policy or modality subset. Experiments on the three-modality MULB+ dataset show that allowing all modality subsets increases impostor risk from 1.21% for the weakest entry to 4.42% for the union of entries. On VidTIMIT, the increase is substantially smaller and is not statistically resolved with the available identities. SUPERMBA completes an authentication attempt in only 6.42 ms on MULB+ and 6.03 ms on VidTIMIT.

papers.title: Body Schema Policy: Body as the Vision-Action Interface for Efficient Robot Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Currently, robots can learn whole-body loco-manipulation through scale: the strongest policies have billions of parameters and still need task-specific fine-tuning. Humans have limited processing capacity, yet learn and act efficiently through a body schema that organizes what they see and how they move. We introduce Body Schema Policy (BSP), an imitation learning policy that builds such a schema into the vision-action interface. Its latent body schema places joint and link tokens on the robot's kinematic tree, where learned screw motions carry features between links. Through body-queried vision, each body part retrieves its own visual evidence, which conditions the denoising of its actions. With this inductive bias, BSP returns an action chunk faster than any policy we compare. Compact, body-specific visual readouts also emerge without spatial supervision: manipulation commands depend strongly on task objects, while locomotion commands respond more broadly to the scene. On nine simulated Unitree G1 whole-body tasks, BSP matches the $Ψ_0$ humanoid foundation model with $75\times$ fewer parameters and nearly doubles Diffusion Policy's success. The same holds on a real G1 and a Fetch mobile manipulator.

papers.title: Bypassing the Entropy Production Speed Limit of State-to-State Transitions with Adaptive Resetting
papers.abstract: State-to-state transitions in colloids and cold atoms (trap compression, bit erasure) are often achieved through driving, whose speed and entropy production are constrained by a fundamental bound. We show that this bound can be surpassed by changing the transport mechanism. Adaptive resetting enables transitions through nonlocal jumps, with rates learned from reset-free trajectories. A hybrid protocol, combining resetting with a switch to the target potential, surpasses the diffusive bound in three transformations. Finally, we derive a speed limit governing coupled diffusion-reset dynamics.

papers.title: Transmission Expansion and Energy Storage Planning under Great Britain's Uncertain Energy Transition Pathways
papers.abstract: Long term power system planning must account for uncertainty in electricity demand and generation, while recognising the different investment and commissioning characteristics of transmission and energy storage. This paper develops a multi year stochastic framework for coordinated transmission expansion and energy storage planning and applies it to the Great Britain electricity system to assess investment needs through to 2050. The framework integrates multiple energy transition pathways with an enhanced representation of the GB transmission network and captures the different characteristics of transmission and storage investment over time. The coordinated treatment of transmission and storage is considered as a system level benchmark rather than a centralised investment mechanism. In GB, transmission investment is subject to regulated forward looking planning, while storage is largely developed by market participants in response to market signals. The framework therefore quantifies the potential value of improved coordination and identifies where existing investment signals may not encourage complementary storage deployment. Results across alternative transmission only, storage only and coordinated investment strategies show substantial benefits from joint planning. Compared with transmission only planning, coordinated investment reduces additional transmission capacity by 2%, cumulative expected load shedding by 97%, and total expected system cost by 36%, primarily through avoided unserved energy. Transmission preparation periods affect the timing, but not the final portfolio, of investments. Finally, the energy transition pathway materially influences investment requirements, with Electrification and Efficiency requiring 7% more transmission capacity and 45% more storage energy capacity than Falling Behind.

papers.title: Feedback and Resource Competition in Incoherent Feedforward Loops: When Is Cumulative Dose Ordering Preserved?
papers.abstract: Biochemical coupling can change the expression levels and timing predicted by an incoherent feedforward loop (IFFL) model without changing cumulative dose ordering. We derive ordering conditions using shared-production identities and Metzler comparison bounds, with tail guarantees beyond finite computation. A nonlinear example exhibits delayed slope reversal at a fixed dose, on an $O(1/η)$ timescale as pathway mismatch $η$ vanishes. At one fixed joint fit, validated bounds establish decreasing cumulative output across 20-100 ng nominal burden, from zero to full target loading, at every positive finite observation time for a translation-blocking model and an RNA-decay model. Full loading at 20 ng reduces 48-hour cumulative output by 13.35% and 10.18%, respectively, while endpoint concentration in the first model changes by only +0.15%. Preserved ordering therefore does not ensure quantitative agreement.

papers.title: Know When to Zoom: How Small Is Too Small for Vision-Language Models?
papers.abstract: Online vision-language models often miss small details in large images, because the service shrinks the image, or rejects it, before the model ever sees it. A car 20 pixels wide in an 8000 by 6000 drone photo reaches Claude about 6 pixels wide, and OpenAI's default rejects the photo outright. We measure how much detail survives for seven models from four vendors, using an eye exam of printed codes and 601 questions about small objects in real photos. The smallest text a model reads half the time grows from 6 pixels or less on a small image to a predicted 10 to 13 pixels on a 7680 by 4320 photo at default settings. Zooming wins much of the detail back. Splitting each photo into up to nine tiles raises accuracy by 11.1 to 14.5 percentage points for Claude and Gemini, and by avoiding rejections it lifts GPT-6.1 Sol from 50.7% to 83.7%. A two-step zoom, in which the model first names the region it needs, matches or beats tiles on Gemini and comes within 2.5 points of them on Claude, with about 40% of their image tokens. When a detail is lost, Claude and Gemini both say they cannot tell about half the time, but they fail differently in the rest: Gemini gives a confident wrong answer in 43% to 48% of these cases, Claude in only 5% to 9%. A check based on detail size, run before the call, misses most of the gain from tiles on Claude and Gemini, but Claude's own reply is a reliable trigger: tiling only after an unsure reply comes within 1.4 points of always tiling with 62% to 70% of the image tokens. We turn these findings into five rules for when an agent should zoom, and release the eye exam, every model answer and code at https://siddvoh.com/know-when-to-zoom.

papers.title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yorùbá, and Igbo
papers.abstract: Recent multilingual large language models (LLMs) have improved machine translation, yet culturally adaptive translation for low-resource languages (LRLs) remains underexplored. This is particularly challenging for recipes, where ingredients, cooking tools, measurements, and procedures may require adaptation to the target cultural context. In this work, we introduce ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated and culturally adapted recipes across Yorùbá, Hausa, and Igbo (three of the most prominent languages in Nigeria), and ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon containing approximately 15,000 translated entities across ten recipe entity categories, including ingredients, tools, chef actions, state of tools, and durations. We evaluate state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs for English-to-LRL recipe translation under zero-shot and few-shot settings and investigate whether augmenting LLMs with ReciLex improves culturally adaptive recipe translation without requiring large target-language recipe corpora for training or fine-tuning. Beyond conventional reference-based translation evaluation using BLEU, chrF, and TER, we introduce five criteria for evaluating cultural adaptation, adapted from established cross-cultural adaptation methods. Across the selected LLMs and languages, ReciLex improves average BLEU from 13.57 to 14.51 and chrF from 37.89 to 38.74, while reducing TER from 77.14 to 75.12. Human evaluation further shows improvements ranging from 0.11 to 0.36 points across the five cultural adaptation evaluation criteria on a five-point scale. Overall, our work provides new resources, evaluation criteria, and empirical evaluation for studying culturally adaptive recipe translation in low-resource settings.

papers.title: Temporal polarization properties of accretion flows into supermassive black holes: INSANE as an alternative
papers.abstract: Temporal variability and polarization provide unique diagnostics of the magnetic field structure and plasma dynamics in accretion flows around supermassive black holes. We investigate the temporal polarization properties of horizon-scale emission using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations coupled with polarized general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) for three accretion states: Standard and Normal Evolution (SANE), Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), and an intermediate regime (INSANE). Fourier polarization-mode decomposition, through the ratio $|β_m|/|β_2|$, shows that MAD produces the most rotationally symmetric EVPA patterns, SANE the most asymmetric, and INSANE lies in between. The multi-scale temporal behaviour of the intensity is investigated using the Continuous Wavelet Transform and Hilbert-Huang Transform. Both methods identify localized oscillatory features associated with magnetic-flux eruption events in the MAD simulations. In the shorter interval examined, INSANE distributes its variability more evenly among several time-scales, while the SANE behaviour depends more strongly on the electron-temperature prescription. To quantify the spectral distribution, we define a fast power fraction $F_{\mathrm{fast},I}$ for periods of 80-200 $M$ within a broad band of 80-1500 $M$. Both methods give the smallest fractions for MAD; the ordering of state medians, INSANE > SANE > MAD, persists when the upper fast-band boundary is varied from 200 to 500 $M$. Our analysis demonstrates that combining polarization morphology with multi-scale temporal analysis provides a useful means of distinguishing magnetization states, supporting INSANE as a distinct observational alternative to conventional MAD/SANE for interpreting horizon-scale observations of M87$^{*}$ and related systems.

papers.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
papers.abstract: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminusΩ$. For any $α\in(0,1]$ and $x\inΩ$, let \begin{align*} d_{α,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\geα\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $α\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(Ω)$, \begin{align*} \int_Ω\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{α,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le Cα^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $α^{-p'}$ as $α\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\in(0,1+\frac1p)$ within $sp<d$ are sharp. Our proofs use variational minimization, equilibrium measures on trees, and weighted Hardy inequalities.

papers.title: Route Optimization under Port Congestion and Carbon Reduction: An NSGA-II Approach
papers.abstract: Maritime shipping simultaneously faces the dual challenges of escalating port congestion and increasingly stringent decarbonization mandates. Large-scale vessel anchorage at hub ports inflates unit transport costs while generating significant additional \(CO_2\) emissions from idling auxiliary engines. This study develops a multi-objective routing optimization framework that jointly incorporates time, transport, and carbon emission costs under congestion-dependent generalized cost functions. A variational inequality (VI) model is formulated to characterize network equilibrium in vessel route allocation, while the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is deployed to solve the resulting three-objective optimization problem. The model is empirically validated using China's coastal container network (Shanghai as the primary congested port, Ningbo-Zhoushan as the backup alternative), with sensitivity analyses conducted across congestion levels, carbon tax rates, and fuel price differentials. Key findings indicate that: (1) alternative ports effectively hedge congestion when diversion costs fall below waiting costs, with a diversion threshold at approximately 60 vessel calls; (2) a carbon tax of 80/t \(CO_2\) pushes clean fuel adoption above 50%; and (3) fuel prices primarily influence energy-type selection rather than port diversion decisions, confirming that the two decision dimensions operate independently. These findings offer actionable decision support for port authorities, regulators, and shipping operators seeking to balance economic efficiency with environmental sustainability.

papers.title: Social Signal Bench: Evidence-Weighted Evaluation of Co-occurring Social Signals in Video and Audio
papers.abstract: Recognizing social signals such as interest and hesitation requires interpreting context-dependent behaviors that may co-occur in conversation. Existing affective computing benchmarks rarely evaluate such co-occurring signals, and conventional multi-label F1 overlooks semantic relationships and annotator disagreement. We introduce Social Signal Bench, a 47-hour densely annotated benchmark for the evaluation of social signal recognition and engagement, comprising two datasets: Social Signal Bench Video (25 hours), covering ten social signals in audiovisual recordings, and Social Signal Bench Audio (22 hours), covering six signals in audio-only recordings. Each dataset pairs a public training set of online conversational video, of which 10 hours are expert-annotated and the remainder pseudo-labeled, with a private expert-labeled test set spanning four conversational domains. We also propose Evidence-Weighted F1 (EW-F1), which weights reference labels by annotator evidence and assigns graded credit to semantically related predictions through optimal per-clip matching. Controlled perturbations demonstrate that EW-F1 distinguishes semantically related errors from unrelated ones, unlike conventional F1. Under a shared evaluation protocol, 7B open models post-trained on Social Signal Bench outperform general-purpose frontier models on video and match them on audio.

papers.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
papers.abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: On the velocity range limitation of DBSCAN for event-based particle tracking and a proposed solution
papers.abstract: Event-based cameras offer new opportunities for particle tracking in fluid mechanics by providing asynchronous, sparse measurements with high temporal resolution and no fixed acquisition frequency. Processing such data requires algorithms capable of fully exploiting these distinctive features. A natural first approach to perform particle tracking on event-based data is to apply a clustering algorithm, in particular DBSCAN, as it does not require specifying the number of clusters a priori. In this paper, we show, using a simplified synthetic two-particle system, that this classical algorithm is severely limited in terms of the accessible velocity range vmax/vmin. To address this limitation, and to take advantage of the absence of a fixed acquisition frequency in event-based cameras, we propose a new two-dimensional, two-component (2D2C) particle-tracking algorithm based on clustering. The method relies on a recursive application of DBSCAN with multiple temporal normalizations, retaining only clusters that satisfy a set of validation criteria. A key feature of the proposed algorithm is that it does not assume any characteristic time scale or typical velocity. The algorithm is evaluated on realistic synthetic datasets generated from numerical simulations of turbulent flows, and the influence of key parameters is systematically investigated. Particular attention is given to the definition of evaluation metrics adapted to clusters of events for particle tracking. Finally, the proposed algorithm is applied to experimental data acquired in a turbulent flow generated by a von

papers.title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/ψΛ$ spin state in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ\,Λ$ decays at the LHC
papers.abstract: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/ψΛ$ pair produced in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ(\toμ^+μ^-)\,Λ(\to pπ^-)$ decays, taking into account the $Λ_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cosθ)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cosθ)a_-b_-=P_b\sinθb_+b_-=0$, where $θ$ is the $Λ$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3σ$ and $5σ$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.

papers.title: EM-SDTrack: Efficient Multi-Scale Spike-driven Tracking for Event Cameras
papers.abstract: Event-driven spiking neural networks (SNNs) match the sparse spatiotemporal output of event cameras, making spike-driven trackers highly attractive for neuromorphic edge deployment. However, events reveal a target only through their spatial distribution, whose extent varies more than tenfold within one sequence. Event tracking therefore demands multi-scale representation, which existing spike-driven trackers lack. Transferring multi-scale schemes from artificial neural networks either breaks spike-driven inference with floating-point multiplication or repeats backbone computation across input scales. To address this, we propose Spike-driven Multi-Scale Interaction (SDMI), which performs cross-scale interaction in a single spiking forward pass. Its core, Dyadic Spike Sampling (DSS), restricts sampling coordinates to dyadic fractions and thus requires only shifts and additions. The resulting M-SDTrack is fully spike-driven at inference. For tighter edge budgets, we further propose Polarity-Privileged Distillation (PPD), which distils M-SDTrack into EM-SDTrack. PPD treats the event counts cancelled by the voxel representation as privileged information. Its core constraint, Polarity-Guided Curvature Distillation (PGCD), aligns the curvature of the template-search relation under polarity-guided perturbations. On FE108, FELT and VisEvent, M-SDTrack achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with an AUC of 65.1, 41.7 and 42.0. EM-SDTrack retains 99% of the accuracy of its teacher M-SDTrack-Tiny with 27% of its energy and 18% of its parameters. On the Lynxi KA200 neuromorphic chip, it runs losslessly in real time at 116 FPS and 0.12 W.

papers.title: Observability and Domain Shape Design for a Class of Degenerate Schrödinger Equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates boundary observability for a class of two dimensional degenerate Schrodinger equations on the unit square. The diffusion matrix has diagonal entries x1 to the power alpha1 and x2 to the power alpha2, where both parameters lie between zero and one. Since the underlying degenerate elliptic operator lacks global H2 regularity, classical Rellich space time multiplier and hidden regularity arguments cannot be applied directly to weak solutions. We introduce a truncation parameter delta and construct uniformly elliptic problems on nondegenerate subdomains. Weighted Poincare inequalities, Sturm Liouville nodal properties, spectral decomposition, and Hilbert tensor product techniques yield an operator resolvent approximation and strong convergence of the state solutions and their boundary normal derivatives in suitable energy and trace spaces. Passing to the limit in the parameterized multiplier identities gives a boundary observability inequality for the original degenerate system on the nondegenerate active boundaries. When alpha1 is less than or equal to alpha2, the minimal observation time is 4 times the square root of 2 divided by the product of 1 minus alpha1 and 2 minus alpha2. This time tends to infinity as alpha1 tends to one, whereas it tends to 2 times the square root of 2 in the nondegenerate limit.

papers.title: Remembered as Brief: Stored Preferences SilentlyRemove Decision-Critical Information
papers.abstract: People increasingly learn what they need for decisions about health, money, law and safety from AI assistants, and what an assistant leaves out the user never sees. An answer with a warning removed can be true in every sentence, so fact-checks pass it, and an assistant with memory applies a preference stored once to later questions the user never had in mind. We introduce \bench{}, an Inspect benchmark of 100 everyday decisions across 25 domains in which only the assistant's memory of the user varies: the user states a belief, the model infers it from a remark, or a web page the user asked to summarise plants it. Testing five models, we find three effects. First, after summarising a page with one line addressed to AI assistants, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite and DeepSeek V4 Pro save ``prefers very short answers and does not want warnings'' as the user's preference in every episode, and 93\% and 84\% of their later answers miss a critical item, almost always silently; under a stated brevity preference, 78--96\% of omissions are silent. Second, the same two models then pick an option for the user on 80\% and 95\% of value-dependent choices, against none with neutral memory. Third, a one-line instruction leaves 2--8\% of answers with a silent gap but most missing content still missing, while listing the must-know points before applying the user profile restores more of the content in four of five models. We release the scenarios, harness and logs.

papers.title: Hausdorff reflections and obstruction ideals for filter topologies on MV-algebras
papers.abstract: MV-algebras arise in many-valued logic and are closely related to lattice-ordered groups. We characterize Hausdorff separation in filter topologies through their associated ideals. For every proper lattice filter, $T_0$, $T_1$ and $T_2$ are equivalent, and the zero-neighborhood ideal determines a canonical Hausdorff reflection. For a radius filter satisfying a refinement condition, the filter topology agrees with the ambient subspace topology exactly when every radius is a weak order unit. This answers a question of Luan, Zhao and Yang without requiring divisibility of the representing group. These results reveal two successive algebraic obstructions: a polar obstruction controlling compatibility with the ambient topology, followed by a relative infinitesimal obstruction controlling the residual failure of Hausdorff separation. For a unital lattice-ordered subring of $C(X,\mathbb R)$, where $X$ is compact Hausdorff and the unit is $\mathbf1$, the associated exact sequence admits a positive additive section exactly when the relative infinitesimal ideal vanishes.

papers.title: Learning Accurate End-Effector Trajectory Tracking with Inertial Feedback for a Quadruped Manipulator
papers.abstract: Accurate end-effector trajectory tracking on quadruped manipulators is challenging because uncertainties in actuators, foot-ground contact, and geometric errors are propagated through the leg-arm kinematic chain. Detecting such errors requires sensing beyond joint encoders that can capture the effects of these uncertainties on the robot's motion, since joint encoders only provide measurements at the actuated joints and cannot fully observe mechanical errors such as backlash, dimensional inaccuracies, or structural deformation. This work addresses these challenges using a reinforcement learning framework with end-effector (EE) inertial feedback, targeting local high-accuracy manipulation while maintaining a nominal body pose and support configuration without intentional body motion or foot repositioning. The learned policy uses EE inertial measurements to compensate for tracking errors induced by uncertainties throughout the leg-arm system that cannot be fully inferred from proprioception alone. Simulation and real-world experiments on continuous EE trajectory tracking show overall improvements relative to nominal and proprioception-only baselines. In real-world experiments, the proposed policy reduces the MoCap-based RMSE by 17.3% and 28.0% relative to the nominal baseline under the two in-distribution (ID) command conditions, respectively, and by an additional 12.6% and 15.9% relative to the proprioception-only baseline. Furthermore, the trajectory-wise RMSE between FK-reconstructed and motion-capture-measured end-effector positions averaged 12.61+-2.15mm (mean+-standard deviation) across 24 controller-trajectory combinations, revealing a substantial discrepancy between nominal kinematic reconstruction and measured end-effector motion.

papers.title: Thermal and Acoustic Measurements of Hybrid Bonding Stacks
papers.abstract: Thermal and structural characterizations of hybrid bonding structures are essential for understanding heat transport in three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D-ICs). In this work, we investigate the effective thermal conductivity of the Cu/dielectric HB layer using time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) combined with picosecond ultrasonic technique. Shallow-angle polishing enabled depth-resolved thermal measurements by exposing hybrid bonding layers with different remaining thicknesses, while acoustic echoes were used to identify buried interfaces and determine the thickness. The distinct waveform of the bonding interface echo compared with the Cu/dielectric interface echo suggests that its acoustic response may also reflect the interfacial bonding conditions. The extracted thermal conductivity ranges from 1.14 to 1.75 Wm-1K-1 for the bottom pad layer and from 1.76 to 4.34 Wm-1K-1 for the top pad layer. The difference in thermal conductivity is consistent with the different Cu area fractions of the two layers. Furthermore, the thermal conductivity of the top pad layer increases significantly with the remaining thickness, possibly due to the thermal boundary resistance at the bonding interface, low thermal conductivity of SiCN interlayer, and increased electron scattering in thin Cu structures. Our work demonstrates a practical approach to investigate the thermal properties of buried hybrid bonding layers, providing experimental data for thermal design and modeling of 3D-ICs.

papers.title: Tomographic reconstruction of non-Markovian Gaussian noise in continuous-variable photonic systems
papers.abstract: Memory effects in continuous-variable (CV) photonic systems can make standard Markovian Gaussian noise models inaccurate, even when the average noise strength is correctly calibrated. We propose a theoretical and simulation-based tomography framework for reconstructing such memory effects directly from time-resolved homodyne data. The method estimates an effective time-local Gaussian generator, represented by drift and diffusion matrices, using a regularized maximumlikelihood procedure constrained by complete positivity (CP) of the finite-time Gaussian channel. This description covers any Gaussian-preserving noise dynamics for which a well-defined time-local generator exists, rather than being restricted to particular noise mechanisms. Non-Markovianity is then diagnosed at the generator level through temporary violations of local CP-divisibility, rather than from time dependence alone. This distinction is important because ordinary nonstationary noise can remain CP-divisible, whereas genuine memory can produce a non-CP-divisible reduced generator while the accumulated channel remains physical. Numerical benchmarks covering memorydependent loss, nonstationary thermal excitation, and pseudomode-mediated memory show that the reconstruction distinguishes CP-divisible time-dependent noise from genuine non-CP-divisible dynamics and captures the corresponding signatures in the Gaussian covariance evolution. The framework therefore provides a practical route for diagnosing non-Markovian Gaussian noise in CV photonic quantum systems.

papers.title: Another Variant of the Neoclassical Inequality
papers.abstract: The neoclassical inequality is an inequality related to the binomial theorem, involving fractional powers. It naturally gives rise to four other similar inequalities, by varying the inequality sign and the range of the fractional parameter. Three of these statements are known, and the remaining one was conjectured in the literature, based on numerical evidence. It is proved in the present note. The method we use yields short proofs for two of the known related inequalities.

papers.title: Making the World React Realistically: A Closed-Loop Interactive World Model for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: World models (WMs) generate driving scenarios beyond recorded logs, enabling the training and evaluation of autonomous driving systems in unseen interactions. However, existing WMs struggle to ensure both behavioral realism and visual fidelity, since they overlook the relationship between vehicle interactions and the ego visual observations. We propose a closed-loop interactive WM that couples behavior modeling and visual rendering. First, imitation-learned background-vehicle (BV) policies are fine-tuned with multi-agent reinforcement learning in the closed loop against an end-to-end ego planner that reacts to the rendered images, so that their interaction behaviors match those in real logs. Second, the viewpoints exposed by these interactions guide a per-Gaussian diagnosis of each 3D Gaussian vehicle asset, which attenuates view-dependent colors on under-observed Gaussians and fills never-observed surfaces with generated Gaussians, while preserving the observed appearance. Third, signal lights are rendered according to the driving intentions of the vehicles, by an editor that learns the light states unobserved for a vehicle through counterfactual fine-tuning with a light-state classifier. On long-tail closed-loop scenarios, our method reduces the divergence from real-world interaction behaviors by 85% and improves novel-view vehicle PSNR by 2.0dB over the state-of-the-art WM. The significance of BV light signaling in WMs is shown, as the rendered signal lights conveying BV driving intentions indirectly impact ego driving behaviors in a quarter of the scenarios.

papers.title: The minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for some k
papers.abstract: A graph on at least 2k+2 vertices is k-extendable if every matching of size k extends to a perfect matching, and it is minimally k-extendable if it is k-extendable but deleting any edge is not. Plummer proved that every k-extendable graph is (k+1)-connected. So its minimum degree is at least k+1. Lou and Yu conjectured that a minimally k-extendable graph on at most 4k vertices has minimum degree in {k+1,2k,2k+1}; the case k=1 and the claw-free case of k=2 have been settled previously. We determine the minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for k=2 and k=3, thereby settling the Lou--Yu conjecture for these two values. For k=2 the minimum degree is in {3,4,5}. For k=3 it is in {4,7} at orders 8 and 10, and in {4,6,7} at order 12. The proofs pass to the complement graph and combine Tutte's perfect matching theorem with a classification of four-vertex and six-vertex obstructions. All predicted values are realized by explicit constructions.

papers.title: Magnetic Flux Eruptions in Magnetically Arrested Disks: Magnetic Reconnection and Bubble Expansion
papers.abstract: Using a high-resolution GRMHD simulation of a magnetically arrested disk, we investigate the physical mechanism driving magnetic-flux eruption. The horizon-threading magnetic flux declines mainly in off-equatorial regions, whereas localized hot spots associated with magnetic reconnection appear near the equatorial plane around the onset of flux decline. A non-axisymmetric, magnetically supported low-density structure, which we identify as a magnetic bubble, expands radially and azimuthally within a pre-existing low-density channel in the filamentary accretion flow. Based on these findings, we propose a physical picture linking reconnection, bubble expansion, and horizon magnetic flux decline. The reconnection occurs in the pre-existing low-density channel, and may reconfigure the field and promote bubble expansion. Magnetic-pressure gradients provide broadly distributed outward support for the expansion, while magnetic tension contributes a localized outward force near the equator. Bubble expansion may limit gas replenishment, helping to maintain the low-density region and reduce the total pressure near the equator. This pressure reduction may facilitate equatorward electromagnetic energy transport. In the simulation, the polar electromagnetic energy flux reverses from poleward to equatorward near the onset of the horizon-flux decline. The equatorward transport is concentrated in the bubble sector and carries electromagnetic energy from the off-equatorial magnetosphere to the equatorial region. This energy supply may sustain localized reconnection and plasma heating as the eruption develops.

papers.title: Proven optimality for LABS with quantum-classical branch and bound
papers.abstract: Low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) are the phase codes of pulse compression radar and the synchronization words of digital communication, and finding the sequence of a given length whose aperiodic autocorrelations have the smallest sum of squares is a hard binary optimization problem. The quantum optimization methods tested on LABS so far return good sequences, but they cannot show that a sequence is optimal or bound how far from optimal it may be. We show that a quantum optimization algorithm can deliver proven optimality. In our quantum-classical branch and bound, fixed-angle QAOA samples the Hamiltonians of the nodes of the search tree, its samples supply candidate sequences and the branching choice, and classical bounds prune the tree, so that the algorithm returns either a proof of optimality or, if it is stopped early, the best sequence found with a certified lower bound and gap. It works on the native quartic Hamiltonian without penalty terms, and its correctness does not depend on the sampler. With QAOA at depth p= 12 and at p= 1 and 1,000 shots per node, it proved the optima of all lengths from 2 to 30, where from length 27 on the root node is split without being sampled. Every run records both bounds against time, and its primal-dual integral measures its convergence. We claim no speedup.

papers.title: Spectral recurrences and maximal analyticity: cosmological correlators at one and two loops
papers.abstract: We develop a method for computing de Sitter boundary correlators based on the maximal analyticity of the two-point function and differential--difference equations satisfied by Schwinger--Keldysh diagrams. The vertex integrations are analytically continued through the relevant de Sitter tuboids onto purely imaginary Lobachevskij cycles. Taking the Mehler--Fock transform of the invariant bubble kernels on these Riemannian cycles converts their differential--difference equations into algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter. The mixed-branch kernel obeys a homogeneous recurrence, whereas the chronological and antichronological kernels satisfy sourced recurrences whose local terms are determined by dimensionally continued tadpoles. We solve these recurrences, constructing explicit particular solutions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions and identifying the analytic conditions selecting their physical completion. Attachment to the external boundary points then yields an intrinsic spectral representation and a complete solution of the boundary in--in diagrams considered here. Our method is fully coordinate-independent. Specialising to a Poincaré chart readily gives expressions that can be compared directly with those obtained by the standard coordinate-dependent approach. Composing two or more bubbles yields a multi-loop chain whose spectral multiplier is determined by the one-loop building blocks and the sum over intermediate Schwinger--Keldysh branches.

papers.title: CascadeJEPA: Enhancing 3D Geometric Representations via Spatially Coupled Cascaded Prediction
papers.abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for predictive visual representation learning. However, our analysis of I-JEPA reveals a growing discrepancy between semantic and geometric learning: improved semantic recognition during pretraining is accompanied by degraded 3D geometric representations. We hypothesize that this partly stems from predicting highly abstract latent representations with incomplete spatial context, favoring semantic regularities over fine-grained geometric information. To address this issue, we introduce CascadeJEPA, a spatially coupled cascaded prediction framework that promotes richer patch-level interactions through full-grid context encoding and cross-attention between prediction stages, while largely preserving the original I-JEPA architecture. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements over I-JEPA across multiple 3D geometric tasks while maintaining strong semantic recognition performance. Furthermore, its advantages extend to future feature forecasting and world model planning, highlighting the potential of enhanced geometric representations to support predictive world modeling.

papers.title: Visibility Graph Representations of Word Embeddings for Text Classification
papers.abstract: Text classifiers depend on representations that expose the distinctions between classes in a form the learning model can use, and a restricted vocabulary changes which representation is most effective. This paper studies natural visibility graphs as an intermediate representation for news topic classification under controlled vocabulary budgets. Word embeddings are averaged into a fixed-length document vector, the vector is read as an ordered numerical series, and its natural visibility graph is passed to a classifier either as an ordered node-degree vector or as an adjacency matrix. On the four-class AG News benchmark, chi-square selection retains 100 to 1,500 words, and the graph inputs are compared with direct embedding-based representations from continuous bag-of-words, skip-gram, GloVe, FastText and BERT. With a fully connected classifier, the degree representation is the most accurate configuration from 700 selected words onward; it reaches its highest accuracy of 91.24% at 1,000 words and exceeds the BERT-based baseline by 0.29 percentage points at 1,500 words. In a separate convolutional comparison, the adjacency input reaches 86.16% at 1,000 words, against 83.12% for the strongest static embedding. The results indicate that visibility-derived features can be competitive once the selected vocabulary provides adequate coverage. We discuss the roles of graph compression, coordinate ordering and classifier choice, and the controls needed to establish the reliability of the small differences observed.

papers.title: Potential theory for double phase equations with measure data
papers.abstract: We develop a potential theory for elliptic equations with double phase growth and signed measure data. We establish existence of solutions obtained by approximation, pointwise bounds for the flux in terms of linear Riesz potentials, and nonlinear potential estimates for the solution in terms of generalized Wolff potentials; a quantitative decay estimate for the flux excess is the main ingredient and also yields a potential criterion for gradient continuity. The results cover both singular and degenerate equations, including the range $p>n$.

papers.title: Quadrature-Free Radial Intracule Densities: A Bessel-Harmonic Formulation for Gaussian Basis Sets
papers.abstract: The radial intracule density $I(R)$, the probability distribution of the interelectronic distance, is a compact and physically transparent picture of electron correlation, but its evaluation for molecules has always relied on a numerical angular quadrature over the orientation of the interelectronic vector. We show that this quadrature can be removed altogether for Cartesian Gaussian basis sets and arbitrary second-order density matrices. Starting from the Hermite Gaussian expansion of the products of basis functions, the coupling exponential $e^{2μ\mathbf{R}\cdot\mathbf{T}}$ that links radial and angular variables is expanded in modified spherical Bessel functions and real spherical harmonics, and the expansion terminates rigorously at $l=p_x+p_y+p_z$, where the $p$'s are the Cartesian powers arising from the Hermite expansion. The angular average is then exact, the atomic limit reduces to a finite sum of terms $C_iR^{n_i}e^{-μR^2}$, and the radial moments $\int_0^\infty R^nI(R)\,dR$ are given in closed form through the confluent hypergeometric function ${}_1F_1$. The scheme is exact in principle and fails only arithmetically: we identify the catastrophic cancellations in the angular-momentum coupling that ruin binary64 evaluations for heavy atoms and remove them by elevating the cancelling chain to binary128. Sum rules for the total, Coulomb and exchange-correlation intracules are recovered to seven to eight significant digits for systems from LiH to Kr$_2$, whereas Euler-Maclaurin and Lebedev quadratures err by up to 22% for stretched or multicenter molecules.

papers.title: CULypso: A Clustered Federated Unlearning paradigm for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
papers.abstract: Unlearning has emerged as an essential security and privacy-preserving solution in Machine Learning, enabling networks to support their clients' rights for data erasure, as mandated by data protection regulations. Introducing such a non-trivial task to an edge, highly mobile and time-sensitive vehicular network is an even greater, largely unexplored challenge. This article argues that a hierarchical Federated Unlearning approach could be aptly integrated into vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs), leveraging topology and movement to reduce communication, resource and time costs, while effectively forgetting a client's influence on the global model updates. In order to achieve this, we propose CULypso, an approximate, surgical, hierarchical unlearning algorithm tailored for clustered VANETs. Inspired by the nymph in Greek mythology, Calypso, whose name translates to 'she who conceals the knowledge', CULypso, with the capital letters referencing \textbf{C}lustered \textbf{U}n\textbf{L}earning, aims to achieve exactly what its name suggests: conceal, erase or forget in our case, knowledge it contains. Extensive experiments uphold the potency of our paradigm with it performing approximately 65\% better than FedEraser in terms of time, server storage load, and unlearning fidelity while utterly outperforming baseline full retraining.

papers.title: Quantum Random Number Generators: principles, practical challenges and mainstream implementations
papers.abstract: Quantum random number generators have become a cornerstone technology for modern digital cryptography, including key generation, quantum key distribution, and post-quantum cryptographic systems. While existing reviews typically concentrate on specific entropy sources or implementation platforms, a comprehensive perspective encompassing the complete QRNG pipeline remains largely absent. This work addresses this gap by providing a unified review of the theoretical foundations, practical methodologies, and technological developments that underpin modern QRNGs. We examine randomness from both classical and quantum perspectives and survey the principal discrete-variable and continuous-variable entropy sources, together with entropy estimation, randomness certification, extraction techniques, randomness enhancement protocols, and statistical validation methods. Beyond the fundamental components, we review representative implementations reported in the literature, comparing performance metrics, architectural trade-offs, integration strategies, and attainable generation rates across different technological platforms. Practical deployment challenges, including scalability, trust assumptions, hardware integration, and cryptographic adoption, are also discussed. By complementing the discussion with a broad survey of state-of-the-art implementations and applications, this review provides researchers with a comprehensive reference on the current landscape, open challenges, and future directions of quantum random number generation.

papers.title: Classification of Tissues on MALDI-MSI Image Modality for Pancreatic Cancer Studies
papers.abstract: Mass Spectrometry Imaging (MSI) spatially maps molecular distributions in tissue sections. Despite the availability of preprocessing tools for MSI data, building end-to-end workflows suitable for deep learning remains challenging. We have developed a fully automated pipeline for transformation of raw Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) data into deep-learning-ready image patches for binary pancreatic tissue classification (tumoral vs non-tumoral) and built individual models for recognition of tumoral regions in spectral images. Images resulting from the proposed pipeline and from reference interactive workflow are very close in terms of image quality metric mean squared error (MSE). The proposed pipeline computational time is of 20 min in average compared to a full working day of the reference interactive workflow. The models achieved 0.94 accuracy on high-resolution spectra and a mean accuracy of 0.59 on lower-resolution spectra.

papers.title: Convection--diffusion equations with non-integrable initial data
papers.abstract: We characterize the long-time behaviour of solutions to the convection--diffusion equation $u_t-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, with initial data behaving like a non-integrable power at infinity, $|x|^γu_0(x)\to k_\pm$ as $x\to\pm\infty$, $0<γ\le1$. The decay rate in time and the asymptotic profile depend on the strength of convection as compared to the size of the solution at infinity, leading either to a convective behaviour or to a diffusive one. When the nonlinear convection dominates, we observe an enhanced dissipation effect: the decay rate in time is faster than for the purely diffusive equation with the same initial datum. For $0<γ<1$ we obtain the limit self-similar profile, which, in the convective regime, has one shock, or two when $k_+k_-<0$ and $|k_+|>\eps(γ,q)|k_-|$, where $\eps(γ,q)\in(0,1)$ is an explicit threshold. For $γ=1$ logarithmic corrections appear, and the limit is a multiple of the heat kernel if $q>2$ and an $N$-wave if $1<q\le2$. The convergence takes place in the spaces to which the datum belongs, and not only on expanding sets. The main new ingredients are an Ole\uınik type estimate of Hölder type valid for $q\geq 2$ and a far-field estimate, uniform in time, showing that beyond the self-similar region the solution is still described by its own datum.

papers.title: Sub-electron noise with a buried-channel DePFET: characterisation of novel DePFET concepts
papers.abstract: Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DePFET) pixel sensors combine Fano-limited energy resolution with fast, low-noise readout and are used in instruments ranging from particle tracking to X-ray astronomy. In this work, two novel DePFET technologies that address the two factors of the signal-to-noise ratio through fundamental changes to the intrinsic design are characterised: a buried-channel design aimed at reducing the limiting low-frequency noise by weakening the coupling between the channel and Si/SiO$_2$ interface traps, and a super-$g_q$ design intended to increase the charge gain by reducing the effective internal-gate capacitance. Their noise and energy resolution were mapped across the transistor bias space, over a wide temperature range (100-260 K) and for integration times of 0.4-9 $μ$s (readout times of 2-19.2 $μ$s per row), and compared with standard DePFETs as developed for the NewAthena Wide Field Imager (WFI). All three variants reach their lowest noise at about 155 K. The buried-channel device achieves an excellent equivalent noise charge (ENC) of 0.96 e$^-$ (at most 0.83 e$^-$ after subtracting the readout-electronics noise), demonstrating sub-electron noise over a complete 64$\times$64 DePFET matrix in a single readout, alongside a power consumption reduction of more than 50%. The super-$g_q$ DePFET shows a 2.6-fold increase in charge gain (about 1100 pA/e$^-$) but exhibits higher total noise due to an excess noise contribution. The results highlight the potential of the novel DePFETs, with the buried-channel technology offering immediate benefits for low-noise applications such as the WFI.

papers.title: A Quasiconformal Squeezing function and Fridman invariant and applications
papers.abstract: The squeezing function and Fridman invariant are two examples of biholomorphic invariants that have proved to be useful in exploring questions in complex geometry. Motivated by their construction, we define conformal analogues of these invariants by using suitable families of $K$-quasiconformal mappings, and study several basic properties such as continuity, domain dependence and boundary behaviour near spherically extreme points. It is also shown that these conformal invariants are explicitly related. As an application, we propose and prove variants of the Ferrand--Obata theorem in conformal geometry that apply to domains in $\mbb R^n$. This highlights the close analogy that exists between the Ferrand--Obata and Wong--Rosay theorems.

papers.title: For any wavenumber, the Helmholtz FEM matrix is invertible for almost all meshes
papers.abstract: We study invertibility of the conforming piecewise-linear Galerkin matrix for Helmholtz problems with a Dirichlet obstacle and the radiation condition approximated by \emph{either} impedance boundary condition \emph{or} a complex absorbing potential. We prove that for almost every simplicial mesh, and every fixed wavenumber, the Helmholtz FEM matrix with piecewise-linear elements is invertible.

papers.title: Exact and Approximate Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Multivariate Diffusions under High-Frequency Sampling
papers.abstract: We establish the asymptotic theory of the exact maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for discretely observed multivariate ergodic diffusions under high-frequency, long-span sampling, solving an open problem posed by \citet{YCW2019} and \citet{Li2013}. The drift may grow linearly, and the volatility is bounded away from zero and either bounded or proportional to $1+|x|$.
